Silksong is a remarkable game, it should set the bar for what all other metroidvanias strive to be.  The world of the game is inviting while still unfolding into an enormous space where every inch is packed with secrets, soul, and genuine care from the developers - the time and creativity put into this game absolutely shows.  It's a beautiful, stylish, and mechanically snappy game with an interesting story and setting to get lost in for countless hours. 

It's important to note the game is demanding in regards to it's difficulty - it's also difficult to thoughtfully criticize this because it caters towards an audience that truly does want a serious challenge; in that regard the game delivers.  However; a handful of decisions made by the developers will become a recurring thorn in the side of the player.  I can't explain them as anything other than deliberate decisions to create a more arbitrarily frustrating experience that needlessly wastes the player's time. 

I would recommend the game in a heartbeat, I will put it on the pedestal that it deserves, but I'll also stress it's not a casual game. There are absolutely other titles that I've enjoyed more thoroughly from start to finish than Silksong, but for people up for the challenge it's a phenomenal game to experience.

Better than Hollow Knight in every way, real masterpiece of a game. Team Cherry cooked here, can't wait for the boss rush mode which is hopefully coming soon, the bosses and enemies, as well as exploration and art design in this game are incredible. All the complaints about runbacks and difficulty are genuine skill issues, there were only 2!! runbacks which I had issues with and enemy difficulty felt balanced in my opinion. People need to realise that instead of ramming their head into clearly strong enemies the game is designed to let you go another way and get upgrades so you can come back later and have an easier time.

When "Tomorrow for sure..." finally becomes the tomorrow you've been waiting for. When that tomorrow becomes today. And then eventually, yesterday.

It's been months now, since Silksong came out. I've rested on talking about it for so long, because it's a big game. It's a lot to digest, to think about...

Was the wait absolutely worth it? You'd think that after all of this time, expectations would be set too high. And yet... Team Cherry did it. They didn't just meet expectations, they blew way past them.

Pharloom is much more "alive" than the kingdom of Hollownest. It has its own culture, and expectations. The exploration of the themes of blind faith, and how systems have been created to exploit people's beliefs... Sheesh.

And at the center of it all, is our lovely protagonist, hero-princess, Hornet. Goddamn, is she the star of the show of this game. It's honestly so, so refreshing and different from the first game to have a protagonist that speaks and gives their own input and thoughts. Her dialogue and interactions are so good. Hornet being an alien to Pharloom's society, and constantly questioning it, and eventually becoming fed up with this society's oppressors, is vindicating, to say the least.

Getting to the gameplay, goddamn Team Cherry was firing on all cylinders with this one. The world design and interconnectedness, I mean, it's a metroidvania, but man they really somehow pushed further than Hollow Knight. And that is, extremely impressive. There's always something around the corner. I got lost for endless hours in this game, getting sidetracked, exploring new places, finding new secrets.

And the difficulty. HOO man, is it here. Just the way I wanted it. This is truly made to be a sequel to Hollow Knight, and it expects you to be familiar with its systems before getting into it. It's a mechanical progression from the last game. Combat feels even more refined, as you're able to pull many new moves and options, befitting of Hornet's nimbleness and expertise in combat. On the flipside, you're more fragile. I like to think of it as a lore explanation, the Knight was imbued with void, which is an inexplicable reality warping substance. Even a half pale being, like Hornet, isn't as strong.

Still, you feel like an absolute GOD when you get into the perfect flow. This game's flow of combat has some of the greatest combat highs of all time. You're given so many different tools and different ways of player expression, it's beautiful. The crest system, with different movesets and properties, and tandem with a player's preferred tools, makes every person's playthrough a bit different. Me? Reaper's Crest for life...

Early game is definitely the toughest, but the entire game is super tough. I know in later patches, they did smooth out a little bit of the early game's roughness, toning down some 2-mask spots to only 1-mask. Regardless, you will get your ass KICKED in this game. The difficulty and tension is all there, this is not a game for the faint of heart. It's a 2D Soulslike, just like the previous game, through and through. Some people may disagree, but I honestly don't think any of the boss runbacks in this game were egregious.

And man, those bosses. Holy fuckin' FIRE. There are so many banger fights and bosses in this game. When I mentioned how they perfected the dance of combat in this game, the bosses are the highlight. There are so many bosses in this game that I wish I could refight. Just like the first game, it is so, so satisfying learning the patterns and getting into a rhythm. There's also no free intangibility shade-dash in this game. So you NEED to be locked in at all times. Sure, there are a few stinker bosses here and there, but that's like, every game in existence. I feel like 90% of the bosses are just like, wow. Banger after banger. I need a Godhome DLC for this game...

The OST of this game... Christopher Larkin... You son of a gun, you did it again! Actually such a beautiful OST, man. Tons of pieces that can get me emotional...

Speaking of emotion, the ensemble cast of Silksong is super lovable. I think Pharloom being alive very much contributes to this. A lot more characters throughout the story have their own agency, their own stories, and motivations that evolve and change as Hornet ventures through the land. You grow attached to people over the first two Acts.

And the requirement to reach the elusive 3rd Act, is to help all of these people. To become a protector of Pharloom. Despite Hornet's outwardly cold and aloof demeanor, she grows to love the people of Pharloom, and so she eventually finds an idea, a solution, to take down their oppressors.

And when that plan comes tumbling down? Your heart is fuckin WRENCHED. It's such a crazy story twist. The whole world has been turned upside down, and suddenly both you, and Hornet, are disoriented, both worried about the state of the cast of characters that you left, and having to contend with a world that's suddenly different, and even more hostile. I actually fuckin gasped when Void started seeping out of the trap the Shamans' laid. It's all so good of a sequence and a transition into Act 3.

Hornet, for all intents and purposes at this point, DOES not need to stay in Pharloom. But she stays anyway, not out of obligation, but out of principle. Hornet wants to right her wrongs, and it further shows that she's grown attached to the inhabitants of Pharloom. I think its just such great character building, mannnn. I love Hornet. The return from the abyss, as the music swells and Enter Pharloom plays is one of the greatest moments of all time. And there's still plenty more peak moments.

The quest of the old hearts further wrenched my heart into two. You get to see the ramifications of Grand Mother Silk's presence onto the land. The snapshots of the past are some beautiful stuff, and also some of the most mechanically difficult parts of the game. The Coral Tower gauntlet is one of those things where it shows you that, even a mighty kingdom at the height of its power, that kicks your ass as a player, still wasn't able to stand up against Grand Mother Silk. It's some awesome gameplay integration with story telling. Side note, the Green Prince's story gave me heartaches for weeks after playing through it. Like, doomed gay bug Yaoi ripped my heart in two, I literally felt horrible falling asleep nights in a row thinking about him.

The Red Memory. God. This is one of the huge reasons why I could never recommend skipping Hollow Knight to get straight to this game. It's such an emotional callback, both for Hornet, and for you as a player. The imagery, and the use of that familiar motif from the first game... God, I just put it on to listen to it again while writing this, and I've got shivers. One of the highest emotional payoffs in a sequel I've ever experienced in a game. Ever. Of All Time.

Combined with the true ending sequence and reading the last journal entry for Lost Lace... God fucking damn it. Hornet is one of the greatest video game protagonists of all time.

I love Hollow Knight: Silksong. Despite overwhelmingly oppressive odds, in a world that seems to be on a path of decay, Hornet embodies hope. Hope for change. Hope for a better future. Hope... that things can be different from Hollownest. And I think Hornet being able to save Lace, is such a beautiful message.

What a godlike game. It blew me away. It's one of my favorite games of all time. Are games art? Well, duh, of course they are. And this game? To me, it's truly a shining example of the beauty of the medium. Thank you, Team Cherry.

Amazing game and wonderful sequel, but with some major design caveats in my opinion.

I've sunk a good amount of time into this game over the last few weeks, and it is truly an enchanting experience. The worldbuilding, soundtrack, visuals, and gameplay (for the most part) all mesh together wonderfully into what is probably the most impressive indie game I've ever had the pleasure of playing. I would reccomend this to anybody who loves platforming, challenging combat, deep lore, and anybody who enjoyed the first game.

- SPOILER WARNING FROM HERE ON, SKIP TO FINAL PARAGRAPH FOR TL;DR -

With mentioning the first game, however, comes my biggest gripe with this game as a whole, which is the approach to difficulty. I found the first game to be incredibly fair with its difficulty through the whole experience. It was very little that I would die in Hollow Knight and feel as if it was anybodies fault but my own. Going into the sequel, I did of course expect the game to amp up the difficulty, considering that the first game is known to be a rather hard game. I actually just finished a run of the first game right before starting silksong, and one thing that I noticed is that the spike in difficulty between games was rather smooth when playing each game right on top of eachother, it felt like a rather natural progression at first. I don't seem to have the same gripes with most of the early game difficulty as others; diagonal pogo is fun, Hunters March really isn't that bad, the enemy arena gauntlets are fun, and 2 mask attack damage enemies din't ruin anything for me. My true one and only problem with the games approach to difficulty became clear to me when fighting the first beastfly.

Silksong at the worst of times seems to take the same approach that FromSoft took when making Dark Souls 2, which is to just throw an overwhelming number of enemies and hazards at the player, creating unpredictable, tedious, exhausting, and sometimes completely unfair gameplay moments. The first beastfly fight is the first boss that does this to you out of a handful to come, it's not that bad, but I did find myself annoyed that I was dying because it felt cheap that this rather simple boss is artificially beefed up by having to deal with a bunch of other enemies flying around the rather small arena. This becomes even more annoying later though in places like Bilewater, where you have to traverse one of the most hostile areas in the game to get to the arena, fight through a gauntlet of enemies, then you can make AN ATTEMPT to learn the boss in front of you. This makes learning some bosses so frustrating, and truly does bog down the experience of what is in all other facets a wonderful video game. This exact thing really drug down my experiences with bosses that in reality I really love, such as The Last Judge and Karmelita, both bosses I would have had a lot of fun learning if the game would actually allow me to go and learn them without giving me a whirlwind of resistance before getting to the phases of the boss I'm unfamiliar with. It is absolutely not fun to enter Karmelita's memory, run to the arena, fight three waves of enemies, go into the boss fight at a health and silk disadvantage, then die in her first phase, rinse and repeat the whole process each time you fail until you finally reach phase 2 and start dying there instead, increasing the length of time that each cycle takes to just FIGURE OUT HER ATTACK PATTERNS. That is not fun, it is incredibly boring and completely sucks the fun out of a really cool, and otherwise well-designed boss.

The final boss fight doesn't have an enemy gauntlet or minions, but still suffers greatly from just throwing too much at you in an unfair way. Phase 1 is perfect, almost everything I enjoy in a boss fight. She has quick attacks that can chain into eachother, and requires you to learn specific movements to avoid getting caught in those chains and attack during her small punish windows, very mechanical, very skill-based, super fun, but then phase 2 starts. Phase 2 has her behaving the exact same way, but now she spawns different arena hazards all over the place, making it completely up to luck sometimes whether or not you can avoid her chains without getting hit by any of the projectiles or tendrils flying out of every corner of the arena, which only gets even FURTHER amplified in phase 3 where suddenly there is so much visual noise on the screen that everything start blending together. Let me finish by saying this, I should not have to turn off screen shake to simply know what the hell is going on during a fast paced boss fight that requires percise reflexes, when I never had to do that for any other part of the game.

- SPOILERS OVER -

Despite most of this review being complaints, it's simply because everything else in this game is immaculate. I don't have much to say in what is great about this game, because almost all of it is amazing, and it's hard for me to do it any justice without saying just go play and experience it for yourself, because if you like action/adventure platformers and metroidvanias, then this is a must-play. it had me in a chokehold for 60 hours in my first playthrough, and I enjoyed (almost) all of my time in it. This would have been a perfect 10/10 score for me, if I didn't find myself somewhat exhausted with the game by the last quarter.

I thoroughly enjoyed Silksong.

Having finally beaten this game (and 100%'d it - technically, there's still a few things I should go back and do), I can safely say this has become my favorite game of all time. I loved the world of Pharloom and getting to know Hornet was great. 

The combat of this game felt incredible. Everything was snappy and responsive, and the new Crests system really helped to differentiate this game from Hollow Knight and expand upon the already-fun combat of that game. I really felt like I got to express my "identity" within the game picking the crests that felt best for me - and even using them like "loadouts" for particular situations like platforming segments versus combat potential. My only "complaint" would be that sometimes there's *a lot* of buttons to be worrying about moment to moment which can lead to some missed inputs from time to time. I'd have liked if the silk skills / tools were a little more spread out. It felt too easy to accidentally throw a tool when I just wanted to do whatever I had on my RB button at the time.

My other complaint relating to combat, however, is the runbacks. Some of these fights had some of the most insane runbacks. To me it felt like it really just interrupted the flow of the fight to die, return to the bench, and have to do some kind of platforming segment or dodge a bunch of enemies risking taking chip damage just to return to the fight. Also on some fights I found myself frustrated just by tiny time-wastes here or there. Like it taking Hornet a good few seconds to sit up from the bench and be playable again. Or certain fights requiring a particular skill usage I won't spoil that makes it take a good 15-20 extra seconds of just sitting there to re-enter the fight. When you're already getting a bit tilted from the fight those few seconds of "please just let me play the damn game again" really start to grate on you.

The platforming felt really good though. Definitely very tough in some segments but finishing them was very gratifying. Don't have a ton to say here other than that everything felt very well-executed for the platforming.

I think my favorite part of this game was Hornet's journal entries. In Hollow Knight the entries being the hunter's that you were revealing was interesting and sometimes entertaining, but it was so cool to me to be learning aspects of Hornet's personality from the entries.

If you don't want spoilers on Hornet's personality stuff I'm gonna be discussing that next here. Her character design is incredible here. I love that she has this incredibly confident, tough attitude. Some of her lines in this game go *incredibly* hard. And then comes the journal. We get to read a lot more about Hornet's softer side here. There's so many remarks about how soft a particular enemy looks and how it's s shame she can't pet them, and even small bits about how a particular bug would have been a good pet in the courts back home. These little bits just felt like I really got to know who Hornet is beyond the no-nonsense exterior. Her reaction to the relic-collector finishing the collection and how she'd appreciate some thanks showed a very "human" side to her too. 

This game differentiated it well from Hollow Knight for me in that I actually got to know the character, versus the Knight being a relatively "blank slate" type character seeing as he never talked so we only got passing moments of any kind of personality if any at all. 

Hornet felt like she was bursting at the seams with personality from every moment we saw her talk. I found myself looking forward to talking to just about every NPC so that I could see what Hornet might say to them and glean just a bit more about her. I'm really looking forward to the DLC so that I get to experience more of Silksong.

Also the art of this game is gorgeous. Fantastic job there, Team Cherry.

I mean, what can I say that hasn't already been said loudly and near-unanimously?

It's great. I spent 60 hours on my 105% playthrough of HK, and my first impressions of HK:S is that Team Cherry took the top off the Maybach with this one. They took their time, drove everyone that played HK at launch crazy, drew a few unkind HL3/GTA6 comparisons, and boy howdy, I got HK for Christmas so I can't really speak for everyone, but it sure seems like it was worth the wait.

My only beef is that HK fans will notice that conspicuously missing from Hornet's repertoire is The Knight's "pogo" (diving plunge). Instead she has a bidirectional, diagonal dive attack, which is great in combat for mobility and (when it correctly tracks the enemy) some fun aerial wombo combos. 

Correctly tracks is kind of the thing. Maybe it was a deliberate choice to throw HK vets off guard, but platforming with the dive attack is jank as hell. If you're less than 15 or more than 45 degrees from directly above your target, so sorry, into the spike pit with you. If you're less than about half a normal jump above the target, so sorry, melee attack (that prevents ledge grabs from connecting as well), then into the spike pit with you. Do everything correct but end up looking the wrong way or crossing over something else the game sees as a target right up until thirty frames after you commit? So sorry, but regrettably we must you into the spike pit.

It's, for a remotely competent player, the first real platforming challenge you encounter, and it just happens to be at a point in the game that's completely linear, so you're going to be doing a lot of runbacks and/or save scums to make it back to your cocoon (at least the cocoon doesn't try to kill you like everything else in this game). I've probably died forty times in four hours, which is par for the course for early-game HK, but my issue was that I wasn't really learning; the jank was still getting me well after I had the mechanics down. It usually wouldn't kill me outright, but this platforming challenge is part of a runback leading up to a lot of freaking combat.

That being said, platforming is largely improved; it's just rough at first (especially coming straight from HK or another prestige metroidvania) when you have no mobility and you're entirely dependent on your environment and pixel-perfect vanilla jumps to get to the next fight relatively unscathed. But the firsts two mobility upgrades you get completely transform the feel of the game, from frustrating and somewhat janky to absolutely graceful and fluid. Even more rewarding is you're all but immediately thrown to the wolves. Hope you got the new mechanics down pat over the past ten mintues, because here comes possibly the most beautifully animated, deeply satisfying boss fight I've ever seen in an early-game metroidvania--or soulslike for that matter (sorry Grundy).

This is a very, very difficult game; I've heard some people say it is *the* difficult game out there today. but what makes the HK games great is as hard, as punishing, as unforgiving as they can be pretty much from the get-go, they are always fair. Expect them to be about twice as chonky as an HK fight, but with a good deal less RNG. The first few boss fights in HK:S and even the mobs are so enjoyable that you're not even mad when you die. Your failure was easily identified, easily understood, and, with practice, easily corrected.

HK:S is the 2D Sekiro in that regard. It's a studio that understands their craft down to the bone doing what they do best at their very best.

And it's absolutely beautiful. The improved graphics, deeper lore, and tighter narrative controls (like the wish system) all make the world feel alive and thrumming with mendacity and wonder. While most of the beloved mechanics are still there (still plenty of backtracks, enough that map markers are the singlemost important early game get if you've smoked yourself stupid over the years like I have), Silksong adds several new ones, most notably replacing charms with three (four?) different item classes. The wider variety of kit means you have even more options than you had in HK for builds. Sometimes they help (emptying a whole clip of throwing knives or traps into a humanoid (insectoid?) enemy might just put you over the top), sometime's they're useless, but it's important to remember that like Sekiro the game's difficulty takes into account all the tools at your disposal, not just your needle and reflexes. Everything I've seen so far has very clear and versatile use cases, but I imagine as you progress further into the game there is more than enough build variety to give you room to innovate without any combo trivializing the game. 

Just because of the dive jank I'm giving it a 9/10. I think if they were to make tracking about 5 degrees 
and 50px more permissive it'd go a long way, but I mean I got gud eventually.

Reading reviews for this game is like reading the Rotten Tomatoes for The Departed; just buy the damn game already.

补充一点想法：
关于跳跳乐：能感觉到tc在这方面是有创新的，雪山的冻伤机制符合环境设定，沙川的限时跑酷很有意思，机枢核心的跑酷也好玩（感觉比白宫还好玩），再加上有飞针，机动性大大提升，跑起来还是很有意思的（我做送肉任务走的蚀阶，一路二段跳+飞针太好玩了）。但问题是什么呢，问题是①有些跳跳乐后面马上接boss战，没有休息的空挡。②跳跳乐路上放会干扰的小怪，这个是最过分的，如果要做的话完全可以做雪山那种纯粹的跑酷关卡，不然也不会有这么多人骂。
关于小怪遭遇战：一编也说了，这个东西已经到泛滥的程度了，比boss战还多。其实我觉得这作的boss有不少挺好玩的，炽焰之父下劈输出+二段跳躲火好玩；机枢舞者节奏感很强演出精彩；第四圣咏团是少见的超大体型boss，很有压迫感，机制也中规中矩。明明这么会做boss为啥要放那么多小怪遭遇战啊，但凡多加点boss呢（当然，记得在boss房附近加椅子，真椅子）。
关于钉子升级：这作给我最大的感觉就是升了跟没升仿佛一样。前作哪怕只是第一次升级，一些路边一条的小虫子直接秒杀，反馈感十足，但这作就没了，甚至我三级钉子砍一些小虫还是要两刀。或许是为了配合9丝回三滴血的机制，所以把小怪的血量也上调了，但综合来看就有点设计失误的意思了。
还是开头那句话，游戏底子很好，但还是有点可惜。


一编：
目前进度在第二章，高庭连战前。最后还是决定给个差评，如果后续体验好一点了可能会改（虽然云了一下感觉也不是很好）

再然后就是假椅子。本来存档点就应该让玩家无条件感到安心，尤其是在这样高难度的游戏里，一而再再而三消耗玩家的信任到底是何意味啊？前作只有一把假椅子而且坐上去只推动剧情不掉血，你丝之歌的假椅子除了侮辱玩家有任何用处吗？

This game is good. If you liked the first game or just like metroidvania's in general, this is an easy recommend. I kinda can't get over how bullsh*t the ending is though.

Assuming you care about side quests, it will probably take you about 50 hours to get to the final boss. The final boss is not even close to being the hardest boss in the game, you'll beat it and get what most people would consider a "bad" ending. The game rolls credits, says "Thanks for playing!" and sends you back to the main menu. In many games of this genre, this is the point where the game reveals what percentage of the map you've uncovered but Silksong doesn't. Silksong is very content to let you have that bad ending and not hint at any other possibility for continuing the game.

When I beat the game, I looked at a complete map of it on a wiki and found that there were four large areas that I never even got a hint of. A game from a major publisher wouldn't allow this. Most devs want you to see all the stuff they made for a game but Team Cherry already got their millions from the first game and they don't give a shit if you don't know how to enter the diving bell at the bottom of Deep Docks.

The tl;dr is: this game is obsessed with hiding secret passages in the ceilings behind some junk in the foreground and you really need to be climbing every wall and checking every weird spot to see if it's solid. It's not La-Mulana bad but it's close.

Наверно мой первый отзыв в стиме. Ставлю Не Рекомендую для привлечения внимания, но в целом мои впечатления на грани + и -. Так что оценка честная. На момент написания этого отзыва я прошел игру на 100% кроме последнего босса трушной концовки. Немного задушнился на ней, но я это добью тоже.

Предыстория - я не большой фанат сильно сложных игр, которые требуют молниеносной реакции молодого Брюса Ли, однако сильно простые игры мне тоже не нравятся. Я люблю некий челлендж. В этом сравнении SilkSong скорее относится к первому - перегиб в сложность. Ну по порядку.

ПЛЮСЫ:
- Игра наследует красивый визуальный стиль из первой части. Шикарная музыка, интересная история и Лор, который хочется познавать.
- Любовно проработанный детальный мир. Он нелинеен. Проходить локации, платформинговые пути и бои можно различными способами в разном порядке, использовать разные способности. В этом плане игра честная, к примеру если удар попал в цель, то не имеет значение ситуация, в которой это произошло - удар будет засчитан. В мире очень много секретов и потайных мест. Эксплорить его хочется, он увлекает.
- Практически нет багов - за все 200 наигранных часов мне попался только один - Хорнет стала невидимой во время побега из бездны (платформинговая секция на время).

ТЕПЕРЬ МИНУСЫ:
- Искусственно увеличенная сложность ради сложности. Средства для этого взяты самые душные и нечестные. Когда я выше писал про честность игры - это было про механики. Здесь же затронем саму идею. 
 * Разработчикам похоже многие боссы показались легкими, поэтому они добавили в некоторые фазы боя призываемых помощников. Призываются они зачастую рандомно, непредсказуемо, дико рассеивают внимание. В результате уже становится невозможно все держать под контролем, и количество попыток боев резко возрастает. 
 * Второй момент - это ГРЕБАНЫЕ телепортации боссов. Это тоже совершенно рандомная, нечестная, непросчитываемая механика (особенно этим напрягала булавочница и Сет) - тот момент, когда ты уклоняешься от удара, и босс телепортируется в тебя, будто он заранее знает, куда ты от него отпрыгнешь (ну конечно знает, только делать так несправедливо). 
 * Зачем делать полумарафонский забег отчекпойнта до некоторых боссов?! Чтобы делая это в 10й раз уже устать, начать совершать глупые ошибки и увеличить количество траев боссов еще на пяток-другой? Душнейшая идея, которая не несет ни прокачки персонажа, ни прокачки скиллов игрока, а просто тратит его время. Первенство тут конечно занимает Великий Гроал, второе место делят Хуемуха номер 1 и Последний Судья. Третье место отдаю Клеверным Танцорам (при условии не открывания шортката). Поучитесь, как такое делать у GRIME. 
 * Ну и последнее про духоту, но не последнее про нечестную сложность - на кой перед боем с боссом делать несколько волн призываемых помощников?! - привет тот же Гроал, и привет Кармелита. 
 * Следующий момент про сложность - зачем отнимать по две маски здоровья, начиная с начала игры? Ну есть там моменты, где одни атаки отнимают две маски, а урон касанием или падение в яму отнимают одну - в этом можно найти смысл, хоть я и не поддерживаю это. Слышал - отнятие по одной маски за падение в яму/лаву/шипы - это нерф позднего патча. Изначально будто весь урон был двоемасочный. Вопрос - заче?? Чтоб игрок подольше помучился и вкусил плоды вашей 7-летней атмосферы разработки?
 * Урон касанием - как же меня это бесило всю игру. Урон касанием - это то, что заставляет тебя вместо того, чтобы экспериментировать и пробовать разные атаки, тактики и оружие и бросаться на врага и получать ФАН (цель любых игр в первую очередь - это веселиться, да-да, веселиться, а не страдать и превозмогать), вместо этого жаться в угол как забитая мышка, и лихорадочно прикинуть, в какие же паттерны можно нанести хоть один удар боссу.
* Расходники для оружия. Тут только про оружие - это каменные чешуйки. Скорость их пожирания во время восстановления оружия сводит на нет все попытки их использования во время попыток боев с боссами. Стоит тут сказать, что если мы говорим про игровую валюту - бусины - то тут в целом я не против того, как это реализованно в игре, хоть и пару раз приходилось чуть погриндить бусины.

- Другой минус - весь третий акт. Из эксплорейшена он превратился в некий мортал комбат - продвижение от одного босса до другого. Небольшая часть карты - бездна, часть дальних полей и Вердания - капля в море поединков с боссами. Да плюс ещё душнейшие, наискучнейшие испытания блох!!! хуже всех боссов! Из-за них я забросил игру на 2 месяца и не хотел возвращаться. 

ИТОГО: Что я люблю в метроидваниях - дух исследовательства - это в силксонге присутсвует (первые 2 акта 100%), нелинейность и возможность решать задачи разными способами, техниками, инструментами - абсолютно правда. Оригиналькая идея, лор, атмосфера - без нареканий. Что я НЕ ЛЮБЛЮ  в метроидваниях - к сеансу игры надо готовиться, как к выходу на ринг/сцену/олимпиаду, надо быть свежим, трезвым, психологически собранным. Игра не расслабляет, игра напрягает, тратит нервы, тратит время, ломает вашими руками геймпады и клавиатуры. А после победы приходит не восторг и удовлетворение, а опустошение. Игра не должна быть легкой, но она должна быть в МЕРУ (ключевое слово) сложной и ни в коем случае не душной.

Ну и пара слов в защиту некоторых моментов, от которых полыхнули другие обзорщики:
- диагональный дэш - это хорошо, ново, интересно. Привыкается быстро.
- цветочки на пути охотника не такие сложные, такими были даже до патча с нерфом их хитбокса
- птички в Греймуре тоже не такие сложные.
- действительно сложные платформинговые места опциональны (кроме побега из бездны и путем за двойным прыжком).

Итого резюме - получил ли я удовольствие? на 50%. Буду ли играть снова? Никогда. Стоит ли игра своих денег? - в целом стоит.

The long awaited sequel to the master piece game Hollow Knight 2017. Team Cherry prove once again that you can make a good game with a reasonable price unlike the majority of the extortionist game companys that exsist. However the game itself has many pros and cons that need to be addressed.
Pros: Gameplay: The combat machinics of hornet are fun and smooth, that perfectly capture hornets boss fight in the first game (always nice to see consistence), while being a nice contrast to the knights combat mechanics from the first game i.e Quick and Stylish from Blunt and powerful. 
World-Building: As expected the world design and mythology is truly a work of art. With Pharloom being a setting thats colourful and vibrant yet errie disturbing as you learn more that displays tema cherry artistic brillaince. 
Characters: Hornet is one of the best video game protagonists ever no question. She was already an interesting character in the first game and due to "the knight" being featureless the narration essiantely focused on her. This game shows her character had more to show with many interesting moments in the game Many of the npcs have there moments as well albiet not as interesting as those in the original.
Cons: Story: Unfortunately is much less interesting than that of the first game with the stack of the first game unfortunately feeling absent in this game. The story therefore feels much less interesting than the first and unfortantely come across as being a drag rather then moving you forward.
Bossess: Whease in the first game there is countless bosses that are intresting and memorable (Knights of Hallownest, Absolute Radience) silksongs bosses come across as blander both in terms of gameplay and narration and feel less unique then there should be.
Difficulty: If you think think the first game was hard this game will prove you wrong, unfortantely the design of the location is small and cramped and due to the combat mechainics of hornet makes game more difficult then it needs to be and thats not inculding the amount of puzzle locations you need to go through that kill the momentum of the game . To put it simply there were trying too hard to be like FromSoftware.
In conclusion i would recomment the game but would warn its more of a slow burner then the first and would not be as replayable as the first. But considering that most games are nowadays unplayable "cough" (Ubisoft, Bethsada) "cough" at the best of times thats still saying something.

I love Hollow Knight. I have recommended it to many of my friends, and have always been a HUGE fan of the metroidvania genre since the beginning of it's development (with Super Metroid and Castlevania SOTN) so I'm very familiar with how these games create these "Oh! I can use this on this door back at the beginning!" situations.

Silksong made me feel nothing but incredible frustration beyond the first few hours. The difficulty of encounters heavily out-weighs the rewards that they guard and never left me with a feeling of satisfaction, rather, I felt like I just got lucky. Perhaps the way I was playing was wrong, but I feel that is actually a failure more so on the design of the game than it is a failure on my part as a player; seeing as how I never got the hint that what I was doing was sub-optimal. Secrets, for the most part, feel pointless. While I love the side-quests in concept, many of them felt more like busy work that elongated my playtime in a game I already was frustrated with, and learning that these quests were required to experience the full narrative was disappointing.

While many of these points are very subjective, I really can't recommend this title solely based on the way the difficulty keeps you from feeling the satisfaction that comes from something like a Dark Souls title. I honestly wish I wish could say that this is like Dark Souls, but Dark Souls actually feels rewarding and this felt like a long, painful, and slow death.

I was a huge fan of the original Hollow Knight and had very high expectations for Hollow Knight: Silksong, which were exceeded to levels beyond what I could have imagined. Everything from the world-building, the storytelling, and the character's stories and motives to the gameplay itself is incredibly well designed and matches what the game was trying to accomplish perfectly. While on the topic of gameplay, I also want to highlight how fluid and enjoyable the movement feels compared to the original Hollow Knight. The bosses are also great because each one provides a unique challenge that rarely feels boring, like a minor inconvenience or like a chore. The platforming is pretty straightforward, so I won't go into much detail about it. While the game is great, I do also want to point out a few issues that I've noticed when playing. The shell shard system is not a bad concept, but in practice it has great flaws, like enemies dropping very few on death and enemies in arenas not dropping any at all. Repairing some tools requires too many shards to keep using them consistently, which can lead to the player not experimenting with new tools and just going for the safer options. Another more personal issue is the 2 masks worth of contact damage that some enemies do, which, while not making the gameplay more difficult most of the time, can make some boss runbacks more tedious and annoying to do. Aside from those two little complaints, I loved everything about Hollow Knight: Silksong. I think it's a great game, i think it was definitely worth the wait.

前作72小时112三门两遍过四门两遍死在仙贝，仙贝王格林四灯左特都过了，本作7小时40分第四次死末代裁决者，猎人小径白耗一小时。这种游戏发售先被舆情骂几个月再冒出来真爱玩家给游戏昭雪的国产剧情案例太多已经非常乏味了。玩得不爽的人只要喷就行了，护的人要讲的话术就得一大堆了，你开始先当舆论受害者让对面白送冰清玉洁称号给你，等过几个月喷的早跑完零人在意这个游戏以后再出来扭曲难不难的事实或者给早跑完的对手虚空戴帽子，耍个十来招最后往这个游戏难度以外的所有地方自信地吹、难度上的话题辩证地吹，等steam寂静一个月终于好评回暖，抛开为什么几个月才回暖不谈，只要慢慢花几个月玩完然后如搞笑春秋笔法评论所述出来代表“真正的玩家声音”，你这个社区又是吹子遍地欣欣向荣昭雪成功了。我看过一段话挺有意思的，嫌菜的人只会嫌比自己菜的。所谓人的本质就是双标自己之上人人平等自己之下阶级分明。想证明自己高贵的闻着高难味道过来等着在社区游龙给每一个boss房打不过兽蝇及其他n位boss跳跳乐跳不动下略n张图的彩笔狠狠一脚，彩笔里面打不过关但是以为地球围着自己转只不过🧠没有意识到自己有多爱这种通晓全地球的感觉的嘉豪竟然打不过这个几无快感的难度游戏那必然狠狠批评的。没有几个人心里没藏着自己的利益关系，谁正确谁冰清玉洁这种儿童笑话骗骗自己得了。
游戏本身就是一代的加强版，除了难度变本加厉，说二代是一代技术力的全面升级是事实。只不过难度大概丝之歌是空洞两倍，恶意的话也就十倍吧。髓骨洞穴小怪一哥两血短前摇冲刺带回头、露头以后被大黄蜂普攻压制也一定会触发，落石经典二伤，铃道虫经典二伤只不过cos大型苔藓冲锋者的难度复活点也离得近所以练手很合理；猎人小径跟远野的精英红蚂蚁招数多的四除了血量性能0.9个蕾丝蕾丝要看哭了，还有它的好哥们蚂蚁又能近战又能飞镖的还吃五下才死，就这俩不谈守小径门的斯卡尔大哥蚂蚁cos假骑士我的评价是非常成功，这个比是猎者小径媲美深巢摸黑的软引导完美告诫你接下来强度很高应该绕行，你快去说钟道兽二伤四个招也是不该打的软引导好吗宝贝，一代引导都有问题这一代路径引导好了些结果难度分布真是爆笑如雷，深邃洞窟开局可达猎者小径你赢大了；远野第四圣咏团经典二伤经典头在天上教你跳跃，虽然空洞1通关了没太久的都能一遍过这东西嫌它菜，不过上下扫地掉落火球+ban地板血还巨厚不会有人觉得肯定比三螳螂简单多少吧，还有也是经典笑话了你跟boss过招进天人形态了神格通达能注意到屏幕最顶上有炸弹能打下来然后你能成功在跟巨型boss打架的时候一点事没有坐气流飞上去还在别人视频发弹幕替笨人操作着急；灰沼飞天全家桶全体唐诗笨鸟四个方向肆意抖动，boss荒沼翼主又是经典飞天冲撞二血，终于来了个地面的剪刀哥仔细一看经典盾戳二伤没事跳两步，相比之下钻地跳脸投戟蜈蚣太阳间了嘻嘻；甲木林没木飞天小标枪抛开不谈经典空中boss修女打过灵魂暴君比难度没有就是要你跳，打一半掉下来美摔我两滴血；蚀阶一哥经典盾构出场带螺蝇地空协同，螺蝇去末代裁决者路上跳跳乐必吃榜刷俩还有钱学森弹道我哭死。初见格林死几十次到最后神居许久未见辐辉两遍过，死这种boss了我知道我是菜死的，只要往格林最后在的方向走它的偷背上挑接火花永远不会打中我，飞天二伤扔弹幕逃离叫小弟前置跳跳乐没椅子一次齐三四个让我觉得我是菜死的吗？钱我觉得是够的，可惜我死一次猎人小径-500块就有点缺，再多死点试试看呢

存档第19小时30分打完高庭连战，21小时17分打完二见蕾丝，六血一钉只有丝之矛跟直针，宝贝。打完我直呼我去这么精致这么爽的boss真是值回票价了然后进去找丝母，上来路上一个下劈失败撞刺上回到地面然后跟我说刚刚敲杆子往上抬升的平台我现在永远够不着了，旁边尖刺台也够不着，唯一的办法就是去拿二段跳。我说行吧那我忍了，打通关之前顺便去雪山逛逛怎么个事再把二段跳拿了。好家伙全程跳跳乐的休息点就几根丝没椅子还塞怪，冰水比深坞岩浆还牛批冻一下回不去继续冻一下，每个小段落不允许任何一次失误不然就是掉血，死了就从南极的椅子开始回北极，喜欢闭门造车你赢了，我去b站看我跑了二分之三已经反胃了，机枢核心还没提呢。这游戏被不推荐是应得的，腐汁泽腐殖渠下辈子去。

最高に楽しかった作品の続編。
今作も高いレベルの操作感とアートワークに前作以上の大ボリュームの冒険が合わさって優秀な2Dアクションプラットフォームの作品になってます。
今作からプレイすることも可能ですが、ストーリーものなので[b]前作である無印Hollow Knightのプレイを強く推奨[/b]します。難易度設計も前作プレイ済前提な気がします。
イライラポイントはあるし、それによる低評価もいくつか見られるけど品質が高すぎるのでちょっとくらい不満があっても満足感は高いです。

[h1]どういうゲーム？[/h1]
虫モチーフのキャラクターたちが住む世界で繰り広げられるストーリー攻略型の高難易度死にゲー。
世界観の雰囲気は可愛いキャラの見た目に反してかなり理知的で荘厳。
メトロイドヴァニアというジャンルで、2Dだけど横に進むだけではなく、通行用アイテムや移動スキルを手に入れて縦横方向に広大なマップを探索していきます。

[h1]虫苦手なんだけど？[/h1]
あくまでモチーフになってるだけで昆虫感はほぼなく、販売ページを見れてる時点で大丈夫です。

[h1]何で同ジャンルでこんなに評価高いの？[/h1]
単純にボリューム、操作感、世界観の総合点がめちゃくちゃ高いです。

[h1]翻訳品質は？[/h1]
前作も良かったですが今作も上手く世界観やキャラクター性を表現できている高レベルの翻訳だと感じます。
僅かに誤字がありますが気付けるかどうかという程度です。

[h1]バグある？[/h1]
基本的にないです。
80時間くらいプレイしてて一度だけボス部屋でボスが出てこないバグが発生しましたが、本当に珍しい体験だったと思います。

It's very rare for me to write a review, but for Silksong I feel compelled to.

To start, the art is stunning. There are some truly beautiful areas in this game with small attentions to detail that make the world feel more alive. Like the small ants carrying away the bodies of defeated foes. The same, if not better, little particle effects with the grass and bugs in each area. Not to mention the flying bugs that go past after you climb out the starting areas. 

The characters are made with such love; not just visually, but their animations, voice acting and overall design make each character so endearing. You'll fall in love with them, even your fast travel bug has one of the most impactful scenes in the game. From playing dice with a lonely bug in a cave, to battling the beasts of Pharloom side by side with a trusted NPC friend you're going to feel at home in these hostile lands. Not to mention an item you get later that allows you to hear all of the bugs singing. Some of the bugs even sing terribly which is somehow more charming.

The music is breath taking. So many tracks have been so carefully and thouroughly crafted to represent each area. Sometimes you'll wonder (in two specific areas) why the music is so sad, and the more you find out about them, the more you'll realize exactly why it sounds like that. The final final boss (two finals on purpose) has one of the most amazing tracks in the game. I get chills just hearing some of the tracks, let alone that final theme invoking such strong emotions.

Speaking of emotions, the story and lore (which I won't go into for spoiler reasons) is so wonderfully portrayed. With some moments that made my cry outright and moments of peak joy and wonder when you piece it all together.

The traversal in Pharloom vastly outmatches anything in any other metroidvania style game I've played, there's always somewhere else to go if you're struggling. There are hidden paths to get to your objectives that are so mindblowingly considered for, it makes the kingdom of Pharloom feel like a living, breathing place. The platforming is brutally difficult on a first playthrough especially but so rewarding. 

The bosses are mindblowing, very often I'd say to myself, "There's no way they can top this boss." Only for the next boss to somehow be even more amazing. You'll never tire of the spectacle.

With all this glaze, it's time to talk about difficulty. I'm on the fence here. On the one hand, I personally do not mind the difficulty but I also understand that some people want to just chill on their couch and unwind after a stressful work day and not want to bash their head against a wall. So if you're not ready for what feels like the fight of your life at times, with some truly brutal run backs and such. Then I'd say it's probably not the game for you. However this is a game that challenges you but also, there's always somewhere else to go that will make what you're struggling with. A new tool or weapon upgrade, sometimes a utility tool that makes the situation easier. 

When it comes to the difficulty: Team Cherry was very particular in how they crafted the encounters, I wouldn't want the game to play any other way. Each enemy, boss and obstacle is teaching you how to play better. It'd be like if I tried to play guitar and got frustrated it still sounded bad after a few weeks. Skill at a new game takes time. It won't be for everyone but I think it's worth it. I do think the game would benefit from having accessibility features like Celeste, where they're actively discouraged but do exist for those to just see where the game goes. But that may ruin the intent behind the design so maybe the "art" is more important here.

All this being said, the game is a steal at the price tag. 
I hope you enjoy your journey in Pharloom everyone!

I would love to recommend this game, because Hollow Knight was such a good game, but this took what was wrong with Hollow Knight and made it even worse. To keep it short and to the point, the game relies more on ambushing and overwhelming than strategic enemy fights.

The enemies on their own are not bad, they each play like mini-bosses with clear tells and vulnerable moments when you go up against them. I actually think the enemies are designed well, and if they were left as that I would probably have enjoyed it more. The problem is, the game forces you to have to deal with multiple of them at once way too often, as an artificial way to raise the difficulty.

It feels like a cheaper way to lengthen the time it takes to get through the game. Add to that that the areas aren't particularly captivating and it feels like a lot of empty space and it makes for a rather mediocre experience.

I also think the difficulty spike is too significant in the second half of the game. That is where the majority of my complaints come from. I actually do enjoy the game before that point. But then navigating becomes more irritating and enemies become more numerous. I see a few spots like this in the Hunter's March but nothing as severe as Act 2.

And getting all the way to that point only to be beaten down repeatedly by what seems like unfair advantages in the enemy's favor makes it very discouraging to want to continue and taints the progress I've made up to that point. And that, I feel, is why I can't recommend this game.

I saw another comment say this too. I came out of challenging situations feeling like "Whew, glad that's over with" rather than "Wow! I did it!" And after beating the game, and attempting to go another round through only to struggle motivating myself to continue playing and not feeling particularly compelled by the story, I have come away from this game feeling disappointed. I think it's worth playing through once, but I also don't feel like you're missing anything in particular playing a game like Dark Souls or Bloodborne, vs this. And I feel like those games do a better job of making those kinds of fights feel more strategic than overwhelming.

Perhaps I'll come back to this, and perhaps I'll change my thoughts, but as of right now, I can't recommend this experience

I recommend playing hollow knight first, it is very similar, and it isn't necessary, but this game begins more challenging and has a sharper learning curve. Like hollow knight it feels buttery smooth mechanically, but I find that it requires a bit more precision, which makes sense considering hornets character. My main nitpick is that it feels more linear in its design early on, but that is offset by the fact that the game seems to reward you more for going to certain areas early using platforming tricks or beating challenging areas. Although hollow knight also did this, it feels more satisfying because as one might guess, doing so is more difficult in this game. The semi-linearity is somewhat to the games benefit in some ways as it allows for the game to establish a more clear plot "thread". There is still plenty of piecemeal lore to reward the explorer, if one enjoyed that aspect in the first, If anything I feel like Silksong has more of it, the presentation is just more balanced, is all. 

Again I feel like I should emphasize, although it can be enjoyed wholly independantly, there are many nods to the first game and I feel this title is better enjoyed second if one enjoys the first. Silksong has been a good sequel so far and in my opinion has lived up to the high bar set by its predecessor. I scarcely doubt that if one tries hollow knight that a person will see it as anything less than the masterpiece it is, and having moved on from that, that they will not also enjoy silksong as well.

Despite the comparisons I also feel like I should mention that despite being similar, I believe Team Cherry did a good job of mixing up how hornet plays compared to the knight as not to feel tediously repetitive after coming from the first title. Enemy designs also feel more complex, which keeps things fresh.

Bom, acabei de iniciar o ato 3 de silksong, mas sinto que, mesmo ainda não tendo finalizado o jogo “da forma correta”, preciso deixar aqui a minha review.

Comecei a jogar silksong logo após ter terminado hollow Knight pela primeira vez e, desde então, vi muitas pessoas dizendo que silksong é mais difícil que o primeiro jogo. E, como alguém que jogou o primeiro pela primeira vez e logo em seguida iniciou o segundo, posso dizer que essas pessoas estão certas. silksong é bem mais difícil que o original, mas cada minuto de progressão é extremamente recompensador: cada luta de chefe, cada upgrade e cada quest concluída.

Sinceramente, não vejo a dificuldade como um ponto negativo, porque sou o tipo de pessoa que sempre defendeu que, se um jogo é difícil para você, ou você não o compra, ou aprende a jogar até ficar bom nele.

No entanto, também preciso ser sincero: silksong me fez passar raivas em algumas áreas e chefes que eu não sentia há muito tempo, desde a época em que estava aprendendo a jogar outros jogos, como dark Souls 1, anos atrás.

Por fim, é um excelente jogo. Para você que gosta de desafios, metroidvania e de uma ótima história, recomendo fortemente que jogue a sequência de hollow knight. Silksong merece todo o reconhecimento que tem.

樱桃已经沉浸在自己的艺术里了（在更新之前更加沉浸在自己的艺术里）。这一代的一些坑人设计饱受争议，但是这些恶心人的设计（比如粪池，一大堆的隐藏墙，突然掉落的石头，比起上一代带有微位移的小怪）却恰恰非常的契合他们想要展示的世界观，最后形成一种虽然恶心到玩家了但却能分辨出来不是故意恶心玩家的奇特体验，反而给了我前所未有的探索感和沉浸感
美术和近乎变态的细节绝对是超越上一代的，抛开超绝性价比，单论质量也是我的2025年度最佳游戏
战斗部分整体提升不小难度，缺少逃课流派；搭配丰富度绝对是不输上代的，给了完全不同的手感，蛮新鲜的
跑图部分我们不谈那些恶意的设计（上文说了），裙子，二段跳加飞针的组合，还有可以钉在墙上的钩锁，简直是爽到爆啊，想怎么跳怎么跳，容错高的离谱，太舒服了，要是小骑士也有以上任何一样对苦痛之路我不敢想是多大的帮助
樱桃社只是把丝之歌作为一个媒介，去讲述一个精彩的故事，丰富的世界观，在没有任何经济上的压力之后，樱桃完全沉浸在自己的艺术里，非常推荐您跟着这几位传奇制作人的步伐，在罐头化，简易性舒适性当道的现在，去慢慢探索这样一个充满诚意，细节，非常有魅力的世界

这是一款非常棒的游戏，主要以收集和探索地图为主并和小部分战斗场景相辅相成。推荐前期用猎手纹章探图，中期用漫游者刷钱，后期用猎手+锯齿环，大后期打雷斯和丝母的时候用伟大的建筑师纹章，建筑师的普通攻击有一小段的位移这就让这个纹章在卡距离普攻的时候手感特别好，最后推荐打丝母的时候一定要带上机械钻头这个道具能让你在丝母赢值的时候直接秒掉（我说4个钻头秒丝母有没有懂的）。那些说丝之歌比空洞骑士难的怕是望了暴躁的毛里克和神居螳螂三姐妹了，小骑士的技能机制确实更适合boos战但是一旦涉及跑图大黄蜂能甩飞小骑士。

Hollow Knight Silksong is a game that does not respect the player’s time, and it is massively overrated. The hype was so extreme that it literally broke storefronts, but after playing it, I do not think the praise matches the experience.

The game is full of frustrating design choices. Wasting an equip slot just to see your position on the map is so dumb. Long, tedious runbacks are everywhere, yet there are no Stakes of Marika style checkpoints like in Elden Ring. If you find a new item and want to try it out, you cannot even equip it unless you are resting at a bench, which discourages experimentation which is why I stuck with one build the whole time.

Progression is also needlessly annoying. To access Act 3, you have to complete a specific mission and then defeat the final boss again. The difficulty is far harsher than the first game, making Silksong far less friendly even for returning players.

I still respect what was accomplished here. It was made by a very small team, and charging only 20 dollars for a game with this much content is generous. Silksong is not a terrible game, but frustrating design decisions hold it back from living up to its overwhelming hype.

Hollow Knight Silksong, это пожалуй лучший игровой экспириенс за всю мою жизнь. 
Если первая часть влюбила меня в жанр метроидвании, то вторая плотно забила собой все оставшееся место в моем сердечке.

Avis jeu terminé.
Silksong est un bon jeu. 

Il possède un gameplay nerveux avec une grande possibilité de build son personnage avec le système d'emblèmes a customiser avec des outils pour vraiment avoir notre perso idéal.

Des décors et personnages magnifiques, tout est beau dans Silksong, même bilesac, le "blightown" de HK.

Les boss sont tous incroyables avec des designs inoubliables surtout les boss marquant (boss de fin d'act, mention spéciale a Trobbio qui a une mise en scène de fou pour un boss secondaire)
Une ambiance sonore aux petits ognons avec des musiques qui vous resteront en tête 

Cependant il contient pas mal de défauts qui entachent le plaisir. des défauts malheureusement trop importants pour les ignorer, et malheureusement ils ont tous le même point commun, la difficulté. Silksong est un jeu dur, mais VRAIMENT DUR, le genre de difficulté qu'on ne peut se permettre d'éviter, c'est un peu dommage quand on le compare au 1er Hollow Knight qui malgré la difficulté n'était pas insurmontable pour le gamer lambda. Ici si vous n'avez pas pas vu un gameplay au minimum ou si vous pensiez retrouver les sensations dHK passez votre chemin. l'hors de la 1ere heure de jeu on sent déjà les soucis avec les 5 coeurs mis a disposition cependant tous les ennemis et leur grand mere infligent 2 coeurs de dégats. donc vous n'avez pas 5hp mais 3 vu que vous mourrez en 3 coups et pour enlever ce passif il vous faudra trouver 2 coeurs supplémentaires parsemé dans des recoins de map que vous ne trouverez qu'avec un guide parce que bon courage pour tous les trouver sans. 

Le parcours est fastidieux mais gratifiant, on ressent l'envie des dev de faire un path of pain du 1er HK sur toute la durée du jeu, et c'est gratifiant. franchement j'ai adoré les phases de parcours du jeu , surtout ceux du dernier act et ceux qui débloquent des upgrades. cependant c'est dommage que Hornet fasse une attaque en diagonale vers le bas durant les 1eres phases de parcours et jusqu'a l'obtention d'une emblème avec un meilleur gameplay.

La progression du personnage est lente voire inéxistante par moment surtout a la fin du jeu, on se retrouve souvent a utiliser la même technique en boucle pour passer des combats de boss trop dur
Hornet n'évolue pas, elle ne gagne pas de niveau c'est votre skill et votre patience qui vous fera gagner. Sauf quand les boss ont 89564hp et les combats deviennent un combat d'endurance pour voir qui brisera l'autre. Arme améliorée a fond on prend trop de temps a tuer un boss qu'on se demande vraiment si on a bien l'amélioration ultime de l'arme ou si on s'est pas foutu de notre geule.  (la mouche méchanique et le poison m'ont sauvé contre 100% des boss de l'act 3) 

Les quetes sont inintéréssantes au possible et n'apportent rien au jeu. on se retrouve a compléter des tableaux de quêtes pour espérer obtenir une amélioration d'arme utile. 

L'absence d'option pour skip les intros de boss, ca semble ridicule mais quand on fait toute une zone pour affronter un boss qui va nous 1shot en 2s mais qui mets 2mn juste pour arriver la bas, bah j'aimerai bien les regagner mes 10s de cutscene. l'absence de banc juste a coté des boss est pas assez frustrant pour justifier le manque de bouton skip nan ?

A vous de voir si vous aimez les jeux difficiles. moi j'ai aimé jusqu'au dernier act ou la finir le jeu semblait plus être une corvée qu'autre chose. sinon jusqu'a la fin du second le jeu est une masterclass



Avis millieu act 3 (review originale)
Le jeu était bien jusque l'Act 3 ou tout deviens une purge.

 Tout fait 2 dégats. faut une maitrise parfaite de Hornet pour espérer réussir les boss de cet Act tellement on sent que les devs ont juste mis une tonne de pv pour rien. hollow knight c'était dur mais au moins on avais un sentiment d'accomplissement a chaque boss. dans silksong on est juste content de ne pas avoir a les refaire. (coucou Florinelle et les arènes de corail)

Suffit de voir les success steam pour voir a quel point le jeu filtre les joueurs avec sa difficulté abusée du dernier act. 
Franchement c'est pas normal de ressentir aucun sentiment d'évolution avec 9 coeurs/10 et l'arme améliorée a fond.

Как для того кто ждал Silksong это игра оправдала все ожидания, боевка стала динамичнее и интереснее, боссы разнообразнее. Карта игры увеличилась в разы, из за этого появились крайне душные локации к примеру Желчноводье, вторая половина Глубоких Доков, естественно Бездна и лично для меня Гора Фей (я ненавижу наличие паркура в метроидвании хотя он обязателен). Прошел 3 секретный акт за 34 часа. 34 часа боли, унижения, радости и восторга от того что именно это я и ждал. Отличия от 1 ХК большие, во первых урон множества существ в Фарлуме, 2 маски у каждого второго крипа это сильно. Во вторых наличие Знаков которые тем или иным образом меняют атаки Хорнет, добавляют свои приколы и т.д. В третьих как и было написано мною сверху это огромная карта. В четвертых добавили систему квестов от разных НПС, да они были и в 1 части, но come on тут это визуально проще и ты знаешь куда идти. И наконец то финальное отличие, за все ныне нужно платить, чего раньше не было. Хочешь отдохнуть? Плати. Хочешь собрать бусины? Плати. Хочешь просто пройти дальше? Плати. Хочешь открыть карту новой большой локации? Конечно плати!

Coming seven years since its announcement, and after endless annoying fanbase speculation, Silksong finally arrived in 2025. Its prequel, Hollow Knight, was a surprising indie hit that combined souls-like difficulty and vague lore, in a 2D metroidvania set in a cartoonish hellscape of bugs. It made huge waves, influencing countless other games after it, and leading to an oversaturated market of metroidvania’s (or even HK-likes, as I’ve heard a few times). Has Silksong gone on to match the hype and change the face of gaming like its predecessor?

According to the sales and awards it’s won, it surely has made an impact. What other game has crashed Steam on its release? However, a lot has changed in terms of metroidvania’s since 2017. Numerous indies have experimented and made innovations with the genre since then. What has Team Cherry done with Silksong to make innovations to the genre they helped make so popular? Apparently they’ve taken everything that was insufferable about Hollow Knight and turned up the dial. Runbacks, enemy gauntlets, and corpse runs are more annoying than ever, and will make you wish you had spent your money and effort elsewhere.

Too harsh? Maybe. There’s still a lot to admire here as a game. The production quality is, like the prequel, stellar. Great visuals, music and controls are all here. Moving “Hornet,” the main character feels super tight. Her downward thrusts, though a bit awkward at first, soon will feel like second nature. The world building here is also incredible. Each area will have its own sets of environmental challenges, and its own index of enemies. Each enemy will have its own set of attacks and maneuvers, that makes it so you can’t blindly rush through things. You will have to think and calculate every action, and learn deeply from each encounter, or else you will suffer greatly.

If you do meet the game on its terms…well, you’re going to suffer greatly, anyway.

[url=https://youtu.be/Ip5pYl-MuYs?si=1HA16RPvaa5Kq3kn]GMTK’s YouTube channel put out a worthwhile video about Silksong’s difficulty,[/url] and observed that a difficult game like this serves three purposes: The game becomes more engaging, it “sells” the aspect of the tough world that you’re in, and it makes you feel more accomplished when you finally overcome a tough obstacle. The issue with SIlksong is, running back to fight the boss you died at isn’t engaging after the fifth time you have to do it. That, too, is also boring. Worse, it’s tedious and completely avoidable.

That’s the biggest thing that bothers me here. So much of the actual playtime here feels inauthentically stretched, and buoyed by choices to make it more difficult than it needed to be. Need to make the area harder? Add in another gauntlet room. Need the boss to be harder? Add a runback, and also have them summon enemies during the fight. Want to get this power-up to hit harder? Take this fragile package to one side of the map to the other, and don’t get hit while doing it. Rarely will challenges make you feel like you’re a triumphant badass. Rather, you’ll just be happy to put it behind you. There is scarcely catharsis.

I can't call this game bad, but I also can't recommend it. There’s numerous other metroidvania’s around the same price point that have come out since Hollow Knight, that are way more innovative, fun, and also challenging. Check out Zexion, Astalon, or Nine Sols if you want a much more solid experience. Otherwise, buy this, and prepare for a war of attrition on your patience.

I'm not exaggerating, to me this is a 10. there are criticisms that a lot of people throw at this game, but I genuinely think that these players don't get it, or simply don't like metroidvanias/soulslikes. Which is fine, but.... The game isn't too hard. The game gives you the ability to change your playstyle and moveset early on in the game, and encourages you to switch it up as the game progresses. For example, one of the late game bosses was giving me hell. I tried over and over again all night, but couldn't defeat her. The next day I decided to change strategy completely and the boss came down on the second try. The way they encourage you to backtrack for collectibles and other items in the later game is unbelievably good. I got 100% item completion with no walkthrough, but it didn't feel like the game gave up all its secrets at the end. it took 115 hours after all. The only gripe I have is that there are SO many cool hiding spots for items that end up just being rosary strands. I wish they would've replaced many of those with more lore tablets. The story and themes are amazing. Coming back to the "Amazon Factory" and seeing one of my favorite NPCs dead in the late game before without me being able to help them honestly made me quite emotional. Religion used as a tool to subjugate, while the leaders aren't even believers - a monetary system that charges you every chance it gets, and then judges you unworthy if you come up short - and the way it informs and recontextualizes plot points from the first game without rewriting the story. If you like bashing your head against a boss over and over until you succeed, or hitting walls looking for cracks, this game is 10/10 masterpiece. It isn't for everyone, but it scratches the exact itch for a lot of people, and it does it flawlessly.

Silksong foi, sem exagero, uma das melhores experiências que já tive com um jogo. Confesso que, nas primeiras horas, eu estava comparando tudo com o que havia jogado em Hollow Knight, mas, conforme a história avançava, fiquei tão imerso e impressionado com a trilha sonora, jogabilidade, NPCs e as demais coisas no game que fui deixando a comparação de lado, o que tornou minha experiência com o game ainda melhor.

Apesar de Hollow Knight ser excelente, eu não senti tanta vontade de explorar tudo no jogo. Em Silksong, essa curiosidade surgiu naturalmente, pois a jogabilidade, os cenários, ambientação, trilha sonora, mistérios e a dificuldade dos chefes me deram muita vontade de explorar cada detalhe.

Sobre a arte e as trilhas sonoras, elas são simplesmente lindas, com destaque para as trilhas de Cogwork Core (1º), Choral Chambers (2º) e Bilewater (3º), além das trilhas sonoras dos chefes, que também são excelentes. Nesse ponto, meu destaque pessoal fica para os Dançarinos Mecânicos, que são meu chefe favorito tanto pela trilha sonora quanto pela luta.

Também não posso deixar de mencionar os NPCs, que são muito interessantes e bem trabalhados, com destaque para Shakra e Sherma, que ganharam meu coração.

Esse é um jogo em que dá para perceber claramente o carinho e o cuidado que se teve durante o desenvolvimento. Meu único arrependimento foi não ter pago o preço cheio (comprei em promoção), pois esse jogo vale cada centavo.

As someone who never played the original Hollow Knight, (I can tell people are going to get rage-baited for me saying that) there are a few things I fondly remember during the time when I purchased and played this game. 1: I was tired of the memes of Silksong and honestly wanted to see what the hype was/if it was worth the anticipation. 2: Reading notices and seeing people, even those who played the original complaining about how hard it is in comparison. (Even though they should've expected something hard. I'm on the team of get good.) And 3: Rushing to finish this game in a week (100% too. Not achievements though, I ain't doing permadeath runs) just to play Chrono Gear on release date (September 2025 had some good anticipated games.)

Despite all the memes and hype, my verdict on the game is that its a fairly challenging metroidvania that does live up to being a good sequel to the original Hollow Knight, if a bit on the overrated side (I once read that some games moved their release date to not be overshadowed by Silksong). The graphics and music really bring out the ambiance of the areas you travel to in a varied amount of environments that range from snowy mountains to verdant landscapes. The gameplay feels slick and effective as it leans more towards a more aggressive approach with fighting enemies while making the boss fights more tense in both style and impact. There is also a good amount of kit building with the variety of crests and tools you acquire throughout the game. I will not lie, it is punishing to a degree, but with enough patience and persistence, it makes it rewarding (Either that or people will start crying for ways to make the game easier like with mods). It is worth the money if you are up for the challenge and is a solid game through and through.

- I think the visuals are much more detailed.

- The tone of the game is significantly different. Much more narrative, less mysterious.

- Combat is AWESOME. You feel like dynamic ninja compared to the original game.

- The music is just as good as the original with the benefit of live instruments being played.

- I think this game will be harsh to learn if you never played Hollow Knight, but was surprisingly easy for me to adapt to as someone who played the original.

- I personally liked the story more in the original Hollow Knight. That's not to say this one is bad though.

I am a fan of the genre and I loved the hell out of Hollow Knight. Over all, a lot of this game is a step up from the previous one—it's more polished, there's so much to explore, and I love most of the mechanics (I know people hate the angled pogo, but I ended up loving it after mastering it). I guess you do have to be a bit of a masochist to love metroidvania games because they are meant to be difficult and punishing, but even I have to admit that spending hours of your day off on a game that deliberately makes you go over pointless, boring routes and defeat annoying small enemies over and over just to get a chance to fight the boss is rather pathetic. 

I have just spent hours trying to defeat [spoiler]Groal the Great[/spoiler] and the thing is, I don't feel like I'm improving at all because it takes so long to just get him to show up, and I already know I can defeat all the little guys before him just fine, but after a point, it becomes tiring and disinteresting so it's hard to keep focus. I love spending hours improving my skills and getting gud, but I can tell you with much certainty that this, is not what it is.

It's such a shame because there are so many great bosses and areas in this game. It's just a few really bad ones that are making it feel like it's a grand waste of time, but it happens enough times in Silksong that I can't, despite how much I actually love this game, recommend it. At the very least not if you have a fulltime job and responsibilities. As a student I probably would have enjoy this more, being able to spend 7hrs+ gaming without much consideration for anything else. Spending what little free time I have just to not succeed day after day is rather daunting.

I will say that I still love this game. I'll leave it for a while so that I can come back to it without being bitter, but to be honest, there are a lot of things I'd rather be doing than spend 5 hours defeating a boss that is 80% menial, mindless sequences and 20% actual challenge.

Я прошел через ад Фарлума, выбил почти все ачивки и готов объяснить, почему эта игра - лучший симулятор выгорания и возрождения.

[b]Почему ты не сможешь оторваться (хотя захочешь):[/b]

[b]- Скамейки - это религия.[/b] Если в первой части ты на них просто отдыхал, то здесь ты на них молишься. Скамейка в Silksong - это единственное место, где мир перестает пытаться тебя расчленить. Но будьте начеку: лавочки тут бывают подлыми, и расслабляться раньше времени - фатальная ошибка.

[b]- Желчноводье - это красиво и подло.[/b] Локации настолько живые, что ты буквально кожей чувствуешь влажность и опасность. Дизайн уровней в Цитадели - это когда ты плачешь от восторга и от того, что не можешь пройти этот чертов экран уже десятый раз.

[b]- Экономика выживания.[/b] Каждая бусина здесь на счету. Система шелковых нитей и инструментов заставляет тебя постоянно рисковать, а потеря честно заработанного капитала заставляет сердце биться чаще, чем на боссах.

[b]- Хорнет - это не Рыцарь.[/b] Забудь про медленный темп. Тут всё про скорость, акробатику и идеальные тайминги. Это не просто бой, это чертов балет со смертью.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Мой итог:[/b] Почти закрытая платина. Единственное, что меня остановило - режим игры без смертей. Я люблю эту игру, но мой психолог пока запретил мне туда заходить.

[b]Вердикт:[/b] 10 сломанных геймпадных стиков из 10. Если готов к тому, что игра будет тебя унижать, а ты - просить добавки, то это твой выбор.

[i]P.S. Однозначно рекомендую, но держите валидол поближе к клавиатуре.[/i]

If you had told me that this game was better than the first Hollow Knight, I wouldn't be sure I'd believe you as the original Hollow Knight was already a pretty damn amazing game, but somehow it is. I don't think this game is actually any harder than HK1 but a continuation of where things left off. There is a much better progression of both exploration and platforming that I think is much better compared to HK1. For example, in HK1, there wasn't actually any very difficult platforming in the game that was required until you had to go through the White Palace. This game is much better at that, as it already begins to test your platforming as early as Hunter's March. From that point on, the game ramps up continuously from the Cogwork Core to Mount Fay. The level design is amazing, mixing a perfect balance of platforming areas woven among areas with dangerous traps or enemies: Areas with a much higher demand for platforming tend to have much easier enemies while areas that have much more difficult enemies tend to adapt the level design on trying to safely navigate through enemies, hazards, or mazelike puzzles. And my god, how crazy is it to feel like you've beaten the game to unlock a second game, only to beat that game to feel like you've unlocked a third game. Madness. The scale of areas in this game is madness.

And it would be remiss of me to not speak of the bosses. Some of the best bosses in the game, ranging from truly inspired to incredibly atmospheric. Bosses are not necessarily harder as the game progresses either, as some opt for the emotional or atmospheric route instead. I felt like over time I even got better and better at fighting bosses leading to the bosses being more complex but not more difficult because I had grown as a player. A lot more bosses in this game tended to have small enemy gauntlets before the boss fight, and I actually think they worked pretty well. These enemy gauntlets weren't typically that difficult and sorta warmed you up for the boss. Of course, there are also enemy gauntlets that are so difficult that they might as well be a boss fight (clap clap). I actually adored this arena as a true test to understanding the combat in the game. It forced me to rethink how I used many skills and tools as well as how I approached offensive and defensive play. I think until that point, I had been playing the game not too unlike HK1, and it worked, but after that point I started playing the game like Silksong.

And finally I wanted to note story, atmosphere, and music. Since these things go hand in hand a lot of the time, I want to group them together. Silksong's story is just as enigmatic as the first HK, but also easier to understand if you pay even a little bit of attention. This is mainly due to the fact that Hornet is actually quite verbose and can explain things, but also from the fact that the themes of religious turmoil and oppression are more resonant with most people than an overgrown alien infection. Of course, needless to say the music is amazing, even more than the first game. I don't need to sing more praises on that regard, but I'm so impressed that new and unique music kept being discovered even when I felt I had explored every area of the game. Much like hidden areas, bosses, and items, Team Cherry isn't shy about making unique music that many players will never even hear. It's a charming element of exploration that is often left out but still very important in adding to the atmosphere of exploration.

Im almost done with the game. I have a few small things to tidy up, then i can go face the final boss (which im sure will take 20 tries). I overall enjoyed Silksong, but its without a doubt one of the most frustrating games ive played. 

Unlike Hollow Knight, pretty much all bosses do double mask damage. I think thats bullshit. Alot of non bosses do it too. Sure, you can heal 3 masks instead of one, but the early game is hell. Once you get some extra masks, its substantially better. It is practically mandatory to run multibinder and injector band. Those make a world of difference. 

There are alot more annoying enemies and areas in Silksong than there were in HK. I liked most areas of HK (white palace SUCKED).  Several areas of Silksong are unenjoyable or at minimum annoying. A mix of alot of environmental BS or enemies that are more frustrating than they need to be. 

I still dont like the back tracking required in either game. Its just a part of these games where you are going to die alot. I dont like running 3-5 minutes back across the map just to try the boss again. Especially when its going to take me 5-10 tries before i can beat it. 

My review sounds negative and it partially is but i still overall enjoyed the game. For all the bad, there are alot of goods to it. Its a pretty decent sized game. Tons of abilities to try, areas to explore. The world feels a little more alive in this game than it did in HK. 

The performance was also flawless. No crashes or issues.

It’s a beautifully designed game. The bosses are PEAK, the areas are PEAK, the story is PEAK, and the music is PEAK.

The new Crest-based gameplay adds a huge amount of freedom in how you approach the game. You can play extremely offensively, defensively, focus on healing, or experiment with many other builds. Because of this, everyone can find their own way to overcome the game’s tough challenges.

The game is fairly linear in its early stages, but later on it opens up and offers plenty of opportunities for backtracking and exploration. If you’re struggling with a boss, there’s almost always something somewhere in the world that can help you overcome it.

It’s simply a better Hollow Knight (not that Hollow Knight is bad or anything).

I’d give Silksong a straight 10/10.

I think anybody who played and loved the difficulty of the later parts of the original HollowKnight will absolutely love Silksong, however if you were a more casual player of the original I can see why this game may be too hard for somebody.  Both games also have parts where you kind of have to aimlessly run around until you find a new secret door and I know some people who really don't like that.

Если не торопиться, пытаясь зарашить босса, то все их механики запоминаются довольно быстро, а некоторых и вовсе не нужно бить самостоятельно, отдав это на откуп амулету, плюющему огнём, именно так я поступил при второй встрече с Лейс, просто прыгая с левой стены на правую. Финальный босс вообще вызвал недоумение, так как он гораздо легче некоторых своих предшественников, например, уж точно легче Первой грешницы, хотя механики у них в чём-то схожи. Тем не менее я не могу поставить этой игре отрицательный отзыв, так как играть было довольно интересно, даже несмотря на тлеющий стул. При этом, если вы казуал, не знакомы с жанром метроидваний или выросли исключительно на мобильном гейминге, точно проходите мимо, эта игра вас уничтожит.

Positives:
+ The artstyle is really really good.
+ Each area is very different and atmospheric.
+ The citadel is insane.
+ The game is like twice the size of the original hollow knight.
+ Hornet is a much more interesting character than the knight who doesn't speak or have feelings.
+ The soundtrack is also very good, choral chambers being one of the best songs.

Negatives:
- There is a huge difficulty spike near the end of act 1.
- The roster of bosses is nowhere near as good as the original game's. It feels like the developers went for quantity over quality with them.
- A ton of the difficult segments of the game don't yield very good rewards. Lots of bosses only give you a tool you never use or just nothing at all.
- Theres no way to refight any of the bosses without starting a new save, so the players just have to wait for some type of DLC for that.
- The rosary economy is poorly handled. You lose ALL your rosaries on death and most rosaries found in the world tend to fall in pits and despawn. The most efficient way to earn them is just farming pilgrims.
- There is no NKG or pure vessel equivalent in this game, again waiting for DLC to bring them just makes the game feel unfinished.

Hollow Knight: Silksong is 8/10. It's a great sequel to a great game, and it does its best work building upon the world created by its predecessor. I particularly loved the combat mechanics that you get to play with when piloting Hornet around. Also, Silksong's soundtrack is fantastic, and whoever decided to give composer Christopher Larkin an orchestra again is a genius (the Widow track is an excellent example of audio wizardry). Team Cherry's creativity regarding the bosses they've come up with is worth complementing, as plenty of the critters you fight offer a cool and often rewarding challenge. 

The difficulty tweak from the first Hollow Knight is something I took issue with. Many of the enemies in Silksong do double-damage, which I wasn't fond of. I also found there to be a lack of polish regarding the quality of some enemies/bosses. Obviously these changes weren't catastrophic to my enjoyment of Silksong (I've completed three endings as of writing this review), but it's worth mentioning. 

I hope the downsides of Silksong I experienced don't discourage you from playing it. This game is great, and if you liked Hollow Knight, I think you should play Silksong. Thanks for reading.
