Это ужасный кусок программного обеспечения, а не автосимулятор.
1. В игре огромные проблемы с производительностью. Графика буквально серая и невыразительная, ничего интересного в этой графике нет, при этом игра не выдает стабильный фпс на средневысоких настройках (5070ti+14600KF). Чтобы получить хотя бы нормальную частоту кадров вам придется включать DLSS и генерацию кадров. А это сильно сказывается на плавности игры и времени отклика.
2. В игре сломанный FFB. В руле нет шин, только подвеска. Кроме этого все настройки разбросаны хаотично, что-то в меню настроек, что-то в настройках самой машины. Вам потребуется изучить гайд по этим настройкам и потом тратить часов 10-15 только на то, чтобы одну машину настроить под себя.
3. В игре явно существуют какие-то скрытые параметры. Например при скольжении машина автоматически переходит на контрруление, как будто игра настроена на геймпады, но ей плевать, что у тебя руль.
4. Физика машин категорически отличается от машины к машине. В то время, когда вам будет более менее приятно ездить на машинах GTO, вы будете плеваться от машин GT3/GTP. В GTP гибрид работает как хочет, как его "заряжать" никто не знает. TC названный в русской версии как ПБС работает крайне прямолинейно, нет настройки точки срабатывания, вам просто обрезают мощность.
5. ИИ плевать на вас, он стремится держаться траектории, бороться с ним бесполезно. Такой плохой ИИ я не видел со времен выхода первой Assetto Corsa.
6. Погодные условия ужасные, никаких плавных переходов, прогноза или чего-то еще. Есть мокрая трасса и сухая трасса. Шины у всех машин либо дождевые либо слики. У Мазды MX-5 должны быть всепогодные, но тут на это забили болт.
7. Мультиплеер у вас будет безбожно лагать. Кроме того, при регистрации на планируемый рейтинговый заезд вы должны будете сидеть и ждать в лобби 15 минут. Включить ожидание в практике? Нет, тут вы этого не найдете. Сидите и слушайте крутой саундтрек (действительно крутой, тут без приколов).
8. Контент в игре есть, но нет баланса. Много исторических машин, но нет исторических трасс. У вас все равно есть нелицензионные версии Имолы, Монцы без лазерскана. Уж можно было бы сделать исторические версии для гонок исторических машин.
9. Ужасное меню. Как после pCars можно сделать такой ужас. Настройка FFB вперемешку с индикацией ввода. Вообще не понятно сходу что изменяется и для чего.
10. Интерфейс ужасен. Миникарту нельзя изменить, уменьшить или сделать видимой всю трассу. А на северной петле миникарта отображается в 5 фпс. Серьезно? У вас лагает миникарта просто потому что длинная трасса? Бред какой-то.
11. Смена разрешения через перезапуск игры. Я не играл в Farming Simulator, но уверен что это особенность движка. И это бред... 2025-ый год. При нажатии кнопки Выход из игры вы будете еще 2 минуты смотреть на экран игры. Почему? Что в этот момент делает игра? Передает мои данные Яну Беллу и Остину Агоновски? Передайте им мой горячий привет.
12. А знаете что делает параметр Автосцепление? Нихера не делает. Даже в режиме "Реализм" на машине Porsche 911 964 вы сможете включать передачи как угодно. Здорово, правда?
13. Столкновения ужасны, я тут даже писать ничего не буду.
14. Штрафы являются какой-то безумной смесью Forza и Gran Tourismo. В автосимуляторе? Серьезно?
15. При каждом входе в меню настройки FFB у вас будет рандомно меняться мертвая зона газа. Круто? А заходить в это меню вы будете часто.
========
Это лишь часть проблем. Я могу перечислять их сколько угодно. Игра продается как готовая, это не ранний доступ, не бета-версия. Это полноценная игра. Все те кто пишут - "патчами поправят", вы серьезно? Вы уже заплатили за игру, разработчикам нафиг уже не надо ничего править. Я на 100% уверен, что в игре используется сгенерированный ИИ код. Это не ИИ-генерация картинок для CoD, это именно генерация кода игры. Это не может быть оправдано и игра должна быть подвергнута забвению.

PREFACE:
Don't get me wrong this game shipped with bugs and poor optimization and should have been labeled an early access game, however I am only recommending this game as I feel the developers will make the necessary changes to make this a good racing game in the future. I think all the negative comments are a result of the hype behind this game which I get as I felt the same way with AC Evo on release. Overall the bones for a good racing title are there but there needs to be significant changes.

AI:
The AI is in an atrocious state. Racing single player is unplayable in its current state as AI has no awareness of the player or other AI for that matter. The AI remain on a single line and don't deviate much. When trying to bump them off line they are like rocks and don't move one bit. When going to make a pass on a turn or straight in some instances they well collide into you sending you off track giving you a time penalty. 

Physics: 
Physics are alright but not full blown simulation, I'd compare them to AMS2. This game rewards smooth driving. Front end of the car feels light and maybe some tuning of the car setup can fix that but some don't know the ins and outs of tuning a setup. 

FFB:
Out of the box FFB is terrible. You'll need to spend a lot of time tuning these setting it took me about two hours to get the setting where they feel somewhat decent. One thing that really irks me about this is that you have FFB setting at the main menu and in the car set up page. Each track you go to you will spend the first two minutes of practice dialing in your FFB setting wasting practice time. This setting needs to be a global setting for each car on the main menu possibly where you select the car. That way it saves for each track under that car and you won't have to focus on it in a lobby. All I had a random game bug where I lost all force feedback which I'm attributing to this game as it has never happened in any other racing title I've played.

Stability:
Game randomly crashes in the middle of a race for an unknown reason. This has happened to me twice and I really can't state why. Once with 16 cars on track racing the MX5 at Sebring School and the other with 38 GT3 and LhDM on Monza.

Graphics:
Honestly graphics aren't a big issue to me as long as the gameplay loop is decent. Graphics are comparable to AC1. It does need a lot of optimization from the devs as there are frame rate issues.

Lack of VR and triple screen support:
I personally am a VR racer. Its disappointing to see that VR support was missing day one. I feel like this is something the developers should of planned for as most sim racers use ultrawides, VR or triple screens. I know its coming soon but I just wish it was a day one feature.

In conclusion, this game is going to need a ton of work in order to get it up there with the likes of AMS2 and AC1. I have high hopes with the modding scene as I know people do amazing work. I personally like the online racing system and hope that it can be the "free" version to iRacing, if not there is always LFM. I feel as if the developers are listening to the community and it seems like they are taking the criticism to heart. Only time will tell.

Ich war mir wirklich unsicher ob ich es kaufen soll - oder nicht. Naja es ist schade dass es nur ein Daumen nach oben und einen nach unten gibt. Denn es ist eher die Mitte aber fangen wir Mal an: 

Fahrphysik: 
Ich bin normalerweise viel in Automobilista 2 unterwegs, aber auch ACC (was mich seit dem letzten Update sehr enttäuscht hat). Auch iRacing habe ich viele Stunden gespielt. Was für mich erstmal positiv ist: ich konnte meinen Fahrstil hier sofort adaptieren und der KI auf 100 im 964 davon fahren. Für mich fühlt sich die Physik richtig an, wenn auch nicht überragend. 8/10

FFB: Anfangs war ich erschrocken, da war nichts. Ich hab das FFB eingestellt und muss es auch weiter justieren. Aber man fühlt prinzipiell alles was man braucht - nur zu schwach. Nicht hilfreich sind die Bezeichnungen der Slider. 7/10 aber schlecht beschrieben und schlechte Grundeinstellung. 

KI: Sehr negativ. Die KI ist völlig rücksichtslos gegenüber dem Spieler. Außerdem fährt die wie an einer Perlenkette, untereinander gibt's kaum oder gar keine Positionskämpfe. Und Fehler machen die auch nicht. Das ist viel zu statisch. Im Regen hat mir gefallen, dass die KI versucht andere Linien zu fahren. Aber das war es auch schon. 3/10. 

Karrieremodus: Schwierig. Da ist nicht wirklich drin was versprochen wurde. Es gibt Geld um Autos zu kaufen, verschiedene Meisterschaften, usw... Aber von Teammanagement habe ich nichts gesehen obwohl versprochen. Es macht dennoch Spaß aber ist eben viel zu einfach. Dennoch aktuell der einzige Karrieremodus im Simracing. Da versprechen nicht gehalten wurden mit Ach und Krach 4/10, sehr schade. 

Modding: jetzt kommen wir zu einem großen Pluspunkt. Die Möglichkeiten, die hier offen stehen, übersteigen alles was es derzeit gibt. Modding ist sehr zugänglich, jeder der den Landwirtschafts Simulator kennt, weiß was einen hier erwarten könnte. Letztendlich ist es auch möglich, dass hier der Karrieremodus völlig umgebaut wird. Ist zwar schade, dass das nicht von Anfang an so ist wie versprochen, aber hier kann jeder das Spiel seiner Träume "bauen". 10/10

Grafik: Leider auch hier enttäuschend. Die Wolken sind eine Katastrophe. Der Rückspiegel sieht aus wie ein Playstation 1 game. Die Wiederholung sieht auch irgendwie seltsam aus. Dafür sehen die Fahrzeuge top aus, auch die Strecken können sich sehen lassen. Aber insgesamt 5/10

Ok, it seems like there are a lot of people jumping on the bandwagon to hate on this game. I believe much of this stems from piggybacking the extremely critical early reviews from a couple of youtubers rather than from actual time spent with the game. Is this game perfect? No. Is this game deserving of such harsh criticism? Also no. In my opinion PMR really is not terribly far off from being a great racing simulator. The game certainly has it's flaws but they are all issues that can be addressed as the game matures so long as the developers put in the effort. 

I have been heavy into sim racing for over a decade now and the things I seek most in a sim racing title are solid ffb, intuitive physics, plenty of setting to adjust and get dialed in just right (seating position, FOV, ffb, input perametrs), multi-usb support, wide range of vehicle types to drive, decent selection of tracks and livable but optimized graphics with smooth gameplay. PMR has most but not all of these as if now. 

Let me first say that I tested this game on a system running a 5700X3d, 5070ti, 32gb ram at 4k with most settings maxed (turned distance settings down to 100 instead of 150, screenspace reflections and volumetric fog one below the highest and with TAA on. Have not yet tried DLSS or Frame Gen. On the ring I was getting roughly 60-65FPS around pits and around 80+ elsewhere. On Bathurst I would fluctuate between 90 and 105. This was with 15 ai cars on Nurburgring and 25 on Bathurst. 

For sim gear I was running a DD2, Pro Sim H Shifter, Simagic Q1 Sequential, simsonn pedals and a Ricmotech button box. ,was pretty straight forward even with multiple peripherals. 

For FFB I was running 90% in game, 0% boost, 0% brake feedback 0% smoothing  and have still been experimenting with headroom setting. 

I tested four vehicles, the 787B Mazda, Porsche 911 cup 964, M3 GT4 E46 and the Porsche 962C. The only one that felt a bit off on stock setup was the M3, the 787B ans 962C both felt very good to drive with informative ffb, definitely not far off from being excellent with the exception of the 787B having a bit too much grip in corners. The 787B also has a pretty poorly rendered cokpit with lack luster textures. 

I did experience trouble with 1 and .1% lows causing microstutters, this seemed to be caused by a lack of optimization causing unnecessarily,mitigate this with graphical adjustments, I haven't tried yet. This was not a constant occurrence but definitely something that must be addressed one way or another. 

The car/track list is not huge but acceptable and should improve with time, the graphics are sometimes very good and other times confusingly ancient looking (like in the case of the 787B cockpit), I expect this to improve in time as well. 

The menus and UI serve their purpose, not much to say here apart from preferring not having to confirm/save every little change made. 

I have not yet tried career mode and I know this is an area many complain about. I am not typically a huge career mode person unless the game has a very engaging and exciting career mode that does not feel repetitive. I do not know of PMR will deliver this experience eventually but hope it will. 

This brings me into AI. The AI are not as bad as everyone makes them out to be but they definitely need work. They have a tendency to clip you as passing by or rear end you as you enter a corner. AI is tricky to get nailed down and I hope the developers can deliver on this as that will play a huge part in a good career mode experience. 

Overall, I enjoyed my first couple hours with Project Motor Racing, I think the driving experience with a wheel  is enjoyable and the game has potential to be great. I do think $60 is steep, but if it were on sale for $40 this game would not be a bad game to buy at all. Even at $60, of the money is inconsequential to you I would say go for it.

UPDATE
With quick patches, this game's flaws are being removed.
 - The major issue most people had was road rage level agression from the AI drivers as they would drive through you if you had the racing line. This is now very rare and in line with most of the sim racing games on the market.
 - The second issue related to this was not having a car radar to know where the other drivers are in relation to you. Well you now have one of those too. And it looks (and functions) like others in the sim market.
 - I had heard people have issues with triple screen not being supported. This has been working for me since launch without trouble. 

 - I have still not entered the online games. So I cannot comment on those. To me this game works well single player and I bought it for that side of the game.
 - Just one last note. Most games lock you into race series lenght of only a few laps where you get no real experience learning a track and often have to start in a random position or at the back. This game allow in the campaign mode to set race's to a full lap count and with a proper practice and qualifying you need to manage your tyre heat for those final fast laps.

This game has more than most and with it's current state. I do not feel it deserves to be abandoned. The developers over promised and needed the public to hold them accountable. They have quickly worked on our concerns and the game really is worth a look. 


ORIGINAL REVIEW
I have actually enjoyed the my time so far in Project Race Room.
I have not experienced any bugs or glitches unlike some others. My system is not top of the line and yet I am able to run the gam at its highest graphical options. 

The cars that I have driven have felt good, or I have not had the skill to drive them. This skill issue is common for me. I heve heard that each car feels different and some are not as stable to drive.  But for me, I have not experienced any issues other than my own lack of skill. When playing the career I would suggest testing out the car you intend of purchasing in a race weekend setting incase it is one what does not fit your driving style (ability) or is poorly inplimented.

I have focused on the career mode. Completing championships and these are quite fun. I would need to explore them further when I start purchasing more cars to race. I do enjoy the options of multiple series to choose from. Though the cost of repaires can bring you into bankruptsy, if you spent all your money on purchasing your initial car.

The physics allow me to catch a slip when I have pushed just too far, but still crash if I am reckless. This is not an arcade game and yet it is the only game which allows my little skill to save myself from time to time. But also know when I am getting into to trouble. I can feel the difference between cold tyres and warm tyres. Where the first few laps of practice/qualifying/race is about warming the tyres. Once they are up to temp I can push right to deeper limits of grip.
Also there are some tracks where I can run the curbs at speed. But I have found another where if I place a wheel on the curb, I will be thrown up onto two wheels. This is my lack of skill and the corner's ripple strip is quite steep.

Negative (Only one for me)
The AI's agression is my major issue with the game. And while sometimes the AI will drive into from agression. The AI are more likely to just drive through you if you have not fully completed a pass. This has changed my driving style, where I am more cautious if pushing for a pass which may only have a 50/50 chance.
To further compond the AI hitting me. I then have to pay for that damage they are the cause of.

While I have not experienced multi class racing. I can see that the small (for racing games standards) competitor limit on races might be a hard no for some drivers. Most racing games I know will have a higher limit than this games 18 (15 on consoles). It is not a concern for me, but I added it here as I know others like busy race tracks full of cars. 

Conclusion.
I do recommend this game to those who want to get into Sim Racing or have a single player style focus like myself. It does have a Multiplayer component which I have not explored. So I can only recommend the single player side. The online play does have a ranking system for each class of car you are driving. This will mean that a driver who is ranked high in slower more precise cars, wont be thrown into the deep end when trying a faster series.

Is it a next coming of Jesus Christ (as many expected thanks to Ian Bell's tweets)? No. Is it a good simracing platform to be built upon with upcoming patches and mods and DLCs? Definitely YES! Does the game deserve all the hate? Definitely NO! People just love to hate on Ian Bell (which is stupid, he owns the studio, he does not do the development). The gamepad control is the second best in any sims (right after ACRally). The wheel control (FFB) can be set-up to be good, if you spend some time setting-it up (or wait for some videos sharing the setups). The cars behave very realistically (even though the grip levels might be a bit lower than expected, but not by much). The driving experience overall is great, it is predictable, controlable and FUN. Does this sim deserve a chance? Sure! Do not get on the hate bandwagon. Try it yourself. You can always refund, if you dislike it, but if you are not a IB's hater, I'd bet you probably won't. Would it have been better if it was called Early Acces for few months? YES! But that does not make it bad game/sim and it has a big potential to get even better with time (and patches). Also once the server issues are solved, it will be best sim to just hop on and race for a few laps with your friends. No payed for custom lobbies, no bullshit ... just pure fun.

P.S.: "For all the haters and driving experts out there - I'm not payed by anyone to like it."

Project Motor Racing – great potential, but feels like full-price Early Access

What strikes me right from the start is how oddly the game is put together. A lot of things simply aren’t clear in-game. The force feedback settings are split across several tabs with names that don’t really tell you what they do, and there’s basically no explanation in the UI. You get dumped into a bunch of sliders with no context – not exactly friendly for a sim that lives or dies on FFB and car feel.

FFB – default = awful, custom = surprisingly great

Out of the box the FFB is honestly terrible. With the default global settings you barely feel any connection to the road; there’s almost no detail and the wheel feels vague and lifeless. The weird part is that just changing the “main” FFB options is not enough – if you don’t touch the per-car FFB tab, you still won’t feel the car properly.

Once you finally discover and tune the extra FFB menu for each car, it becomes a completely different game. With some tweaks in that per-car window the detail suddenly appears and you can read what the car is doing very clearly – for me even better than in AMS2 (and I’m a big AMS2 fan). When it’s set up right, the tires loading up, grip building and falling away, and weight transfer all come through really nicely. The problem is getting there: the defaults are bad and the UI does nothing to guide new players.

Tires and car behaviour – good, but very inconsistent

Tyre behaviour is often very good, but also very uneven across the content. Some GT3 cars feel spot-on and really pleasant to drive, others feel like the tyres are permanently under-heated and never quite “switch on”. Hypercars are another strange case – I often feel more grip on cold wet tyres than on warm slicks in the dry, which is the opposite of what you’d expect.

Older cars, once the FFB is dialled in, actually drive really nicely and feel believable. I’m comparing all this against modded Assetto Corsa, LMU, AMS2, AC Evo and ACC – PMR can absolutely hang with them at times, but then you jump into another car and it feels like a different physics engine.

Graphics and performance

Specs: RTX 3080 Ti, i7-11700K @ 4.6 GHz, 64 GB RAM. Performance for me is totally fine.

Visually it’s… weirdly inconsistent. Sometimes the game looks genuinely great – golden hour lighting with strong contrast can look better than AMS2 (even with ReShade) and occasionally comes close to AC Evo. But as soon as it starts getting darker, something odd happens with the lighting. Colours get muddy, contrast goes strange, and it can suddenly look worse than AMS2. Depending on time of day and weather you either get “wow, this looks nice” or “what happened to my shaders?”.

Penalty system – basically a joke

After playing LMU, where the penalty system is genuinely excellent, PMR’s system feels like a placeholder. As far as I can tell it’s always the same +2 seconds whether:
	•	someone punts you off,
	•	you lose it on your own,
	•	you slightly cut a corner.

There’s no nuance, no proper incident handling – it’s either no penalty or +2s for everything. For someone focused on online racing, that’s a big red flag.

Menus, UI and options

I prefer the cleaner modern UI in LMU. PMR’s menu looks like a hybrid of something from the 2000s with a bit of Evo flavour sprinkled on top. It’s still nicer than AMS2’s UI, but it doesn’t feel cohesive.

Another oddity: options sometimes pretend not to save. You change a value, the game clearly reacts to the new setting, but when you reopen the menu it looks like it hasn’t been saved. So the behaviour is right, but the UI feedback is wrong – confusing and unpolished.

Verdict

Since patch 1.5.01, the driving characteristics of some cars have improved a lot, and the default FFB is now noticeably better out of the box – but it still really needs per-car tweaking to shine.

When everything lines up – a “good” car, tyre behaviour in its sweet spot, lighting that works for the track and weather – Project Motor Racing can feel and look genuinely excellent and absolutely compete with the big sims.

However, in its current state it still has a strong “full-price Early Access” vibe:

you have to tune the FFB to get the best out of it,

tyre behaviour is better than before but still inconsistent between classes and specific cars,

the lighting can swing from “wow” to “what is going on here?”,

the penalty system is improved after 1.5.01, but still miles behind LMU in terms of nuance and racecraft awareness.

A lot has improved after patch 1.5.0.1, so now it’s a matter of seeing what the future brings and whether the devs can deliver on the full potential of this sim.

If multiplayer ends up with healthy, long-term population, I can absolutely see myself staying with PMR for longer and treating it as one of my main sims.

For players who enjoy experimenting with settings and don’t mind spending time dialing things in, it’s already a qualified yes – there’s a lot of potential and moments where it really delivers.

For people who just want to jump in, avoid menu fiddling, or mainly race hypercars, it’s still closer to a no for now – a title to watch, maybe revisit in some time, and hope it grows into the sim it clearly wants to be.

Do not bother reading all the overwhelmingly negative reviews of impatient ppl who are not able to learn something new and sacrifice some time to fine tuning the FFB. 

Here is the honest and super-objective review the only one you need to read:
This is a sim, very dependant on tyre model, temps, wear and track grip. You need to learn, set up your car and tune your FFB settings, before it starts to be fun. In certain conditions (cold tyres etc.) the real cars are very harsh and difficult to drive as well. This game is for those looking for a serious SIM. This is NOT an arcade game. If you are not patient enough to learn, do not buy.

Game in its current state is not perfect. AI and penalty system need to be fixed.
Graphics is good but no HDR.
Sound is the absolute best, all the cars sound like the real ones, you can hear all the noises of breaks, tyres etc.
Handling and physics is very good, feels like a proper SIM.

Career mode is a disappointment. I like the idea of financial management, but it is very shallow, I was expecting something much more sofisticated than this. No trophy room, no achievment collection, no care about the cars durability, no R&D, no care about the staff and mechanics, no contracts, basically no team management. At least we have the opportunity to win some championships, which is completely abcent in all other sims. Shame, but still better than just attending a single super-boring race weekend like in LMU. 

In conclusion - serious SIM racers only, the rest will probably hate it.

C’est peu de dire que cette simulation (PMR) était très attendue. Les premiers retours des « simtubers » (qui avaient eu accès à une pré-release) ce week-end étaient plutôt négatives : déception, énorme daube, rien qui va, j’en passe et des pires.
Sortie officielle ce mardi et j’ai pu commencer à tester cette version 1.0 en début d’après-midi. Soyons clair, je m’attendais au pire et mon niveau d’espérance n’était donc pas très haut…

Bon, je n’ai pu rouler qu’un peu plus de 2 heures dessus, c’est donc très léger pour se faire un avis définitif et structuré. Mais, de ce que j’en ai vu, c’est acceptable en solo avec zéro adversaire (en clair, vous êtes seul sur la piste) : le FFB est assez moyen mais pas autant catastrophique que ce que j’ai pu entendre ça et là. La physique semble un peu chatouilleuse, surtout avec des voitures à faible appui. Les graphismes ne sont pas à tomber par terre mais, par beau temps et de jour (de nuit sous la pluie, faudrait voir…), ça va encore. On connait mieux mais c’est pas horrible.
En fait, le problème général de cette V1, c’est qu’elle n’est pas du tout optimisée (et ça peut se comprendre, le titre vient juste de sortir !). Et dès qu’on met des adversaires sur la piste (je me suis contenté d’une douzaine), ça devient à peine jouable. PMR se met à ralentir à tel point qu’on peut se retrouver à rétrograder un rapport de trop tellement le décalage est perceptible.

Je n’ai roulé qu’à Daytona et avec peu de voitures (Porsche GT1 , BMW LMP et Porsche 917). Mais il est clair qu’il va falloir attendre avant que cette plateforme soit utilisable.
Et si jamais on la compare à AMS2, c’est le KO direct au premier round (dès les premières secondes même !). Bref, je conseille d’attendre un peu (tout comme pour Assetto Corsa EVO).

Neues Update 3, wird immer besser!

Its hard to recommend this game in its current state. PMR is very hit or miss in basically every aspect of the game. 
Some cars feel decent to drive while other are borderline undriveable (at least on controller). The cars also tend to lose traction on the rear while youre braking and they overall behave as if they only have full traction or none. 
I havent encountered major performance issues beyond the occasional shader compilation stutter. However, considering how dated the game looks, I expected much higher fps. 
The carreer mode is just underwhelming. You cant change the difficulty after starting the carreer, theres barely any team management and basically all playstyle options rely on winning/getting podium except one. The ai also is questionable at best. They arent aware of where you are and drive on the same line, which is very apparent when you race on a wet track. There also is no option for a rolling start. 
The multiplayer has been also very hit and miss for me so far. The scheduled and ranked events just dont work for me, you either get an error or nothing happens when it starts. Custom lobbies are oversimplified. You basically need to create a new lobby whenever you want to change the class or track (or at least i didnt find an option to change it). Besides that, the ability to create a lobby or join a lobby is pure rng at this point in time. Some people can join/create lobbies while others cant. 
The game also lacks polish. The most obvious bugs havent either been found by the QA or the devs didnt bother to fix them before the release. For example, you can move every part of the ui except the virtual mirror, which is placed in honestly one of the worst places by default. You can put your cockpit camera outside of the car or in some other weird places like the engine bay or trunk. I also managed to launch myself into the air and then fall through the map. 
This game also doesnt have a radar for some reason. 

TLDR: It doesnt do anything new and is very mediocre in every aspect. Lacks passion and should have at least had one more year of development.

The physics and FFB are good, the cars are not "floaty" (an LMU fanboi attack with no merit.) Those reviews which say anything different show a lack of knowledge of how to set up their wheel base for each title.

HOWEVER, the game is a DO NOT BUY.
1: The graphics are poorly optimised,
2: the user interface is a mess (it switches between gamepad and PC inputs on a whim),
3: the game leaks both RAM and GPU memory
4: no MSAA or MLAA option (TAA is utter garbage for racing simulators, MSAA is the preferred choice - old but not obsolete!),
5: badly implemented shadows,
6: badly implemented LOD,
7: badly implemented wheel options,
8: no barrel reprojection for wide screen (it takes about five minutes to add it to the final processing shader but they did not!),
9: MULTIPLAYER DOES NOT WORK AT ALL,
10: and the inclusion of "mobile" settings shows this game was never meant to be on a PC.

I am sure it will improve just in time for PMR2 to be released. Keep your money and wait for PMR2.

Fantastic car roster, decent starting track selection, and a driving model that shows real sim-racing potential. The force feedback can be inconsistent, the AI needs work, and there are noticeable performance and polish issues that make it feel unfinished at times. It absolutely should have been an early access title. That said, when everything clicks, the driving experience is genuinely fun.

I don't understand why the reviews are so harsh for this game.

There is a lot that needs fixing or improving in multiple areas and these issues to detract from the overall experience currently. Areas that need significant improvement are AI, force feedback feel and weight, multiplayer server browser and server configuration options.

That said, I have found the driving experience to be great fun despite the current limitations. Once connected to a server (I've only run a private server with a few friends) the net code has been pretty reasonable (with low ping connections).

To summarise, yes there are issues currently but they do not detract from the driving experience significantly for me. I'm sure issues will be fixed given a little time.

Największym problemem tej gry jest jej strona techniczna. Wymagania rekomendowane wskazują kartę RTX 3070, tymczasem grając na RTX 4070 Super z włączonym DLSS, przy ustawieniach dalekich od maksymalnych, doświadczam spadków do 40–50 klatek na sekundę (bez frame generation). Do tego dochodzą ciągłe ścinki i freezy. Ostatecznie straciłem cierpliwość, gdy po 40 minutach wyścigu na Nordschleife gra zawiesiła się na około 30 sekund, po czym nagle wyrzuciła mnie prosto w ścianę. W takich sytuacjach brak możliwości przewijania jest prawdziwym gwoździem do trumny.

Tryb kariery również rozczarowuje. Po zapowiedziach spodziewałem się czegoś na poziomie trybu kariery znanego z serii F1. W praktyce otrzymaliśmy jednak prosty symulator zarządzania budżetem, w którym ścigamy się bez większego celu. Nawet ciężka praca i zwycięstwo w wyścigu nie są nagradzane krótkim przerywnikiem filmowym czy choćby pucharem. Brakuje jakiegokolwiek zarządzania zespołem, rozwoju siedziby, pojazdu czy kierowcy – po prostu nic z tego, co mogłoby nadać grze głębi.

Sztuczna inteligencja przeciwników to kolejny zawód. Samochody AI są jak przyklejone do swojego toru jazdy. Nie popełniają błędów, nie wyprzedzają się nawzajem, a podczas wyścigu praktycznie nic się nie dzieje. To sprawia, że rywalizacja jest pozbawiona dynamiki i emocji.

Model jazdy na kontrolerze jest przeciętny. Nie jest tragiczny, ale też nie zachwyca. Na temat rozgrywki z użyciem kierownicy nie mogę się wypowiedzieć, ponieważ nie miałem okazji jej przetestować.

Podsumowując – nie polecam. Gra ma niewiele wspólnego z tym, jak była reklamowana. Rozczarowuje zarówno pod względem technicznym, jak i w kwestii zawartości.

Superb physics, amazing tracks, and faithfully tuned cars, sounds like a perfect mix, right?
but throw in bad AI, graphics that look bland and obsolete (mostly even worse than Project Cars 2), bad optimization, and postpone the "essential" features like VR support and triple screen support (the quote representing the priority of the features comes right from Ian Bell, CEO of Straight4 Studios) and the result turns into something much worse than what anyone expected.

It might be a great sim already, but there is so many things blocking you from truly enjoying it, so it doesnt even matter how authentic simulation it provides.
It has potential to be truly amazing, but it still needs a lot of work, it would be understandable if it launched in Early Access, but going with the "Microsoft route" of releasing an unfinished product, and selling it as complete finished product is already pretty bad, calling day one patch as  patch 1.5 is just adding salt to the injury, and topping it off with PR message to the Community, which just does not seem sincere - presents surprise on issues, that you would have to be blind to not see; and it offers some vague promises.

keeping this review positive, just cos I believe into this game, and it has potential to be one of the best racing sims, if not the best one, but now it would deserve a negative review.

And the grace period for the GT3s is now gone. They're back to being kinda mushy and slip abuse seems to be a thing for real this time.
In 1.5.0.1 they went the right direction by addressing slip abuse on the GT3s and they were really pointy, almost reminded me of AMS1 to some extent but with a softer response when you went over the limit. Staying on the limit was hard but it was clearly faster for the most part, abusing slip to go fast was still possible but the gains were minimal in most cases but the same applies to AMS1 and AC1. Doing big slides was too easy, but slower.
They're not terrible now, I still prefer these GT3s over iRacing or LMU even, but they were made "softer" for some reason while all they needed was to make peak slip a little wider so the car didn't go into grip loss as quickly, but now they went too far which how much grip you retain when you go well over the limit.
At least downshifting and being at low RPMs is now possible with most classes without the car snapping out of control, but the LMDh still take a good second to rev up from idle to max RPM in neutral...
I find it quite amusing how no one has noticed this yet, how lazy the LMDh's engines are.

[/list]

Another rushed out, soulless and mediocre cash grab attempt within the racing sims scene. As if things weren't bad enough with Rennsport already here we have yet another project full of promises and potential delivering absolutely nothing. This game needed at the bare minimum another 6 months of development to be ACCEPTABLE (not good, just acceptable).

It needed to be labeled as Early Access and launched at half the price. That alone would have saved you a lot of the negative reception. I actually really enjoy the driving in this game, it had me smiling many times. I use an Xbox controller and it detected it easily and the setup feels good to me. 

But there are huge issues. The AI is terrible. Not much needs to be explained that hasn't already. They drive in a straight line with no awareness at all other than to charge forward. 
The graphics are okay, not very pretty at times and sometimes quite nice. The skybox can look very blurry and ugly during day time races, the clouds look pretty bad in particular. 
Optimisation is not great. I have a 4060 and Ryzen 5 5600x which exceed the recommended specs and I have to rely on DLSS with FSR to achieve decent frame rate along with passable visuals. Frame rate jumps around heavily and the flickering of objects can be distracting. The wheels on the cars do not look very good at all either in motion. 

All in all I can get by these issues if the game wasn't advertised the way it was and was so disappointed with the bare bones release of it. It's really more of an early access game and it shows. I am leaving it as negative even though I really think the game is a very low "Okay". It has huge potential and I do not want the developers to give up at all. I will keep playing in the meantime as well. This game can only go up from here and I believe in the team behind it if they can take the feedback and start working hard on bringing out what they really wanted to.

EDIT: I truly do feel there is a good game to be had here and based off of how the devs are respondin, I think this game can become great. So for that I will be changing my review to positive.

It's been a bit of a shocking launch for PMR. The hardcore sim community are tearing it apart, and that's fair given the promises that were made leading up to launch, and the actual state the game released in. The thing is, if you're looking for a simcade that leans more toward "sim" than "cade", PMR is an excellent candidate! To me it feels a bit like a spiritual successor to the Need For Speed: Shift games. 

Played on a controller with assists on, the racing is thrilling, the visuals are good, and the single player career mode is challenging! There are some things that need fixing sooner rather than later - The AI are insane and will run you off the track if you try to overtake them on the inside of a turn; the penalty system is stupid and will penalise you every time you leave the track, even if you were having a crash or lost places; and the AI difficulty is wildly variable depending on the track and conditions. 75% AI will thrash you on some courses, and get left in your dust on others. The first two issues are already on the dev's radar, so should hopefully be resolved soon.

If you are looking for a competitive multiplayer racer, PMR is not that yet. It needs a few months of patches. If you're looking for a more serious take on the Need For Speed franchise, PMR will do that right now.

Edit: as of today, the AI are fixed and drive far more like professional racing drivers, and the penalty system has had a slight rework to include warnings. For single player career play on controller, there is no better game on PC today. I plan to try it out in my sim rig soon, but until I've done that I can't comment on how the game feels when using a wheel.

Po Premierze: 
Czekałem na ten symulator z ogromną niecierpliwością, hype był ogromny i projekt zapowiadał się jako benchmark dla innych. Niestety, wyszło jak wyszło – hype przyszedł i poszedł, a rozczarowanie zostało. Momentami czuję się wręcz okłamany. Według zapowiedzi mieliśmy dostać wspaniałą grafikę, fizykę dokładną jakiej jeszcze nie było, zmienną pogodę i AI jakiego jeszcze nie było. I tu muszę się zgodzić – tak ślepego AI jeszcze nigdy nie widziałem. Niezależnie od tego, ile miejsca zostawię, przeciwnicy zawsze we mnie wjadą, co sprawia, że w 90% przypadków nie jestem w stanie ukończyć wyścigu.
Grafika jest nierówna – czasami wygląda jak z roku 2010, a przecież mamy 2025. Fizyka i feeling samochodów są bardzo różne: starsze pojazdy prowadzą się nieźle, ale wszystkie nowe, takie jak GT3, GT4 czy LMDH, są nieprzewidywalne i kiepskie w odczuciu. Force Feedback często jest martwy, kompletnie nie wiadomo, co dzieje się z przednimi i tylnymi oponami, jakby zmiana masy czy ciężaru samochodu w ogóle nie istniała. Do tego dochodzą jeszcze śmieszne nazwy niektórych torów – „Brionza” zamiast Monza – co budzi pytanie, czy te tory faktycznie zostały zeskanowane i dlaczego nie mają pełnej licencji.
Na plus mogę wymienić jedynie szeroki zakres samochodów, kilka naprawdę dobrze wykonanych modeli, możliwość wybrania pory roku (szkoda ze nie ma to większego wpływu). Fajny efekt jak się wyjedzie po za tor oraz szybkie czasy wczytywania wyścigów. Nie zwróciłem gry, bo przekroczyłem limit dwóch godzin, testując różne pojazdy. Będę aktualizował tę opinię w miarę pojawiania się nowych aktualizacji.



ENG version: 
After Patch 1.5.1
Pros
- AI has become smarter (it sticks tightly to its racing line, but is able to overtake you even at high speeds — sometimes resulting in the AI going off track).
- Most older vehicles can be driven without changing the default setup.
- Driving classic cars is genuinely fun.

Cons
- AI seems to have its own physics — some cars feel glued to the track.
- Graphical bugs (snow/rain falling through the roof or windshield).
- Short draw distance for objects, visuals look like something from around 2010.
- Car sounds are monotonous, almost copy-paste across all vehicles.
- The game lacks a clear identity: Simulator or Arcade?
- Advanced setup options and tire management suggest a simulator.
- However, the handling of some cars is overly simplified, breaking the overall consistency.

After Release:

I was waiting for this simulator with great anticipation, the hype was huge and the project was supposed to be a benchmark for others. Unfortunately, it turned out the way it did – the hype came and went, and disappointment remained. At times I even feel deceived. According to the announcements, we were supposed to get stunning graphics, physics more accurate than ever before, dynamic weather, and AI like we had never seen before. And here I must agree – I have truly never seen AI this blind. No matter how much space I leave, opponents always crash into me, which means that in 90% of races I’m unable to finish.
The graphics are inconsistent – sometimes they look like they’re from 2010, even though it’s 2025. The physics and car handling are very uneven: older vehicles drive fairly well, but all the newer ones, such as GT3, GT4, or LMDH, feel poor and unpredictable. Force Feedback is often completely dead, leaving me with no idea what’s happening with the front or rear tires, as if changes in weight or mass didn’t exist at all. On top of that, there are the funny track names – “Brionza” instead of Monza – which raises the question of whether these tracks were really scanned and why they don’t have full licenses.
On the plus side, I can mention the wide range of cars, a few models that are actually well made, and fast race loading times. I didn’t refund the game because I exceeded the two-hour limit while testing different vehicles. I will update this review as new patches and updates are released.

[h2]As much as I feel there could eventually be something here, currently this cannot be recommended.[/h2]

[h2]Review in Detail[/h2]

[b]Cars[/b]
The feeling of the cars is not great for a lot of them. Some feel good but for the most part its not quite there.
The selection of cars is good and I love the different classes, I just wish they felt nice to drive. Some feel completely uncontrollable.

[b]Multiplayer[/b]
There is a lot of work needed here from an ease of use perspective.

Its great that we can set up custom lobbies. But why do I have to close the lobby and create a new one when after a race we want a different track, or car, or ANY setting of any kind?
There needs to be the ability to change these from within the lobby. To me this is an absolute BASIC idea and I don't know how it was overlooked.

The ability to run laps in practice or enter car setup while waiting for people to join would also go a long way to remove the feeling of constantly waiting in menu's.

There have been some inconsistencies with lag but this happens with all new games so mentioning it but expecting it to be resolved.

[b]AI[/b]
Apparently the devs have made some of the most advanced AI in racing games. I just wish it was in this game.
The AI cars behave ridiculously.
They will drive through you, not caring you are there. After you have been smashed in to a wall or spun out, if you are in their way, they still wont care despite you being stationary and will smack in to you.
In multiclass races the faster cars end up just forming a line behind the slower cars. Very rarely do they seem to realise overtaking is a thing they can do.
Given the single player campaign is a huge draw, this is a major detractor.

[b]Penalty System[/b]
Touched grass? 2 seconds.
Rammed by blindfolded AI following a predetermined line and sent to the barrier? 2 seconds.
Spun out and taken 30 seconds to come back BEHIND where you left? 2 seconds.
.... if you are lucky. Instead, you might be told to drive at 60kmh for a number of seconds which actually ends up being WORSE. But if you dont do it, 10 seconds.
The penalty system doesnt care about the reason you went off or if you gained time. You are penalised no matter what.

[b]Tuning[/b]
Not all of us have a photographic and encyclopaedic memory.
Having a description of what the tuning settings do when you are on the tuning screen would make it much better for people learning or just the general user. Also which direction makes what kind of change.
Forza and RRE are both good examples of having these explained but you get nothing here.

[b]Controls[/b]
Something is off with the controls. Not that its uncontrollable, but something isnt right here.
The FFB can be made "better" by following Youtube videos but there is no base setting with ANY kind of feeling in the game. Each individual car needs every option tuned.
There should be some kind of basic setup in place just to allow the most simple kind of feeling. Out of the box you cant feel how much grip you have or when you lose it.

[b]Throttle[/b]
I dont know if this should fall under controls or Cars so its here.
What is going on with the throttle?
I refuse to believe that on a slight incline [i]a high powered race car[/i] will roll backwards while in gear with the clutch engaged even if throttle is at 0. BUT these cars will still roll backwards even over 1/3 of the in game throttle indicator showing being pressed.
This means there is very little nuance to pressing the throttle as there really isnt much going on until after 1/2 and usually 2/3 of the throttle.

[b]Final Thoughts[/b]
I am really hoping the developers can bring their vision to life and deliver something even remotely close to what they have promised but it will take a lot of work.
I want to believe in their passion and with how a few of the cars drive I can see that it may be possible but there is a lot to do and a lot of things that will need to be changed along with some things that are just frustrating.

I hope that through the updates things change that allow this to become positive.

Having put 8hrs into this on the first day, I am enjoying the game and have no major problems. I just do race after race with all the interesting different cars. It is a lot better than it is being made out to be. The only obvious problem is the AI but that will be improved. At the moment you just have to give a lot of space when passing as they will just drive the race line whether you are there or not.
I have the game running constantly at 90fps at 3840 x 2160 with a 4080S. The GPU is running at 70 - 80% at mostly high settings. I had to go from 60 to 90fps to overcome a slight stuttering effect in the long distance scenery.
There are a lot of complaints about non issues. I became accustomed to the menus after 30mins and can find whatever I'm looking for. The wheel FFB isn't important to me but with a few tweaks from suggestions on YTube it feels adequate. 
The following is based on the GT1 class. I would describe the handling as forgiving. The car is not floaty it feels connected. The sense of speed is very high and the forgiving handling has the effect of you are more focused on carrying speed through the corners and extracting maximum speed through the racing line. Its exciting to drive. Is it the most realistic? I don't know. Driving a same car and track comparison on AMBS2, the AMBS2 car felt very slow but the handling was more detailed.
This is not the next step forward in racing titles but is a good and interesting game nonetheless and should only improve in time.

Ich war anfangs ehrlich gesagt skeptisch – die Rezensionen, Tests usw. 
Trotzdem habe ich es mir geholt und kurzes Fazit: So schlimm ist es absolut nicht. Im Gegenteil – das Spiel ist wirklich gut.

Ich habe es mit dem Controller gespielt, und genau da liegt meiner Meinung nach der Knackpunkt:
Mit dem Pad fährt sich das Spiel überraschend angenehm, rund und "entspannt".
Wer einen Sim-Racer sucht, den man auch mal locker vom Sofa aus mit Controller fahren kann, ist hier goldrichtig. Gibt sonst keinen außer GT7. 

FFB:
Zum Lenkrad kann ich noch nichts sagen – das habe ich bisher nicht getestet.

KI:
Motorsport ist ein Kontaktsport, und genau so fährt sich auch die KI.
Sie lässt immer gerade genug Platz, aber eben auch nur so viel wie nötig.
Da berührt man sich mal, da schiebt man sich mal, mal gewinnt man das Duell, mal verliert man’s.
Mir macht die KI richtig Laune:
Das Feld bleibt oft eng zusammen, mit ein paar Ausreißern nach vorne oder hinten.
Dadurch entstehen wirklich spannende, lebendige Rennen, die sich nicht wie eine sterile Hotlap anfühlen.

Strafensystem:
Ist übermotiviert – keine Frage.

Grafik:
Absolut ok! kommt nicht an Evo ran, ist aber besser als AMS2 & iRacing. 

Sonst so:
Braucht feinschliff. Wolken sehen teils sehr komisch aus (schwarz) , Text im Menü überlagert sich, Karriere könnte mehr Emotion brauchen (z.B DTM Race Driver 3, Kontrahenten, Videos o.ä). 





Klugscheißer Tipp zu KI: 
Wenn die KI komplett Quatsch macht, liegt das in vielen Rennspielen nicht an der Grafikkarte, sondern an der CPU.
Die CPU berechnet KI-Verhalten, Physik, Kollisionsabfragen und das komplette Fahrzeugfeld – und wenn sie am Limit läuft, reagieren die Gegner spät, fahren unruhig oder verhalten sich unlogisch.

Einfach mal den Taskmanager nebenbei offen lassen:
Wenn die CPU auf Volllast ist → weniger Autos auf die Strecke packen.
Das entlastet das System, die KI fährt sauberer und das Spiel läuft insgesamt stabiler.
Passiert übrigens auch bei ACC, AMS2 usw.

I really wanted to like Project Motor Racing, but in its current state, it’s impossible to recommend.

I’m running a 5070 Ti on a 49" OLED at 1440p, the game suffers from heavy stuttering and poor optimisation. For a title priced like a premium sim, this level of performance is simply unacceptable.

Visually, the game doesn’t match its price point. The graphics feel a generation behind, and definitely not on par with established sims in the same price range.

Gameplay-wise, the issues continue:

AI is inconsistent and often behaves like an early alpha.

Car physics feel undeveloped, floaty, and disconnected from the road.

Overall, the whole package feels like a beta, but for some reason priced higher than fully established sim racers.

In its current state, Project Motor Racing lacks the polish, realism, and stability expected from a full release. Maybe it will become something good down the road, but as it stands today, it’s simply not worth the asking price.

Dear Development Team,

I am writing because the current state of Project Motor Racing is not just disappointing — it is astonishingly below the level that was promised and expected.

Graphics Quality:
The visuals look outdated in a way that is difficult to understand for a game released in 2025. Compared to competing titles, PMR feels visually years behind.

Performance and Frame Rate:
Even with modern hardware, the game struggles to maintain stable performance. Frequent frame rate drops make the experience feel rushed and unpolished.

Career Mode:
The career mode is extremely barebones, consisting mostly of simple text screens. It feels as though this feature was barely started, let alone developed into something meaningful.

Artificial Intelligence:
The AI behaves like something from 25 years ago — unpredictable, unrefined, and incapable of delivering believable racing. It is difficult to imagine how this passed internal review in its current state.

Missing Features (e.g., Pit Radio):
Key features that are standard in modern racing simulations, such as pit radio communication, are missing entirely, adding to the overall feeling of incompleteness.

Pre-release Statements vs. Reality:
The way the game was promoted — especially in interviews by the lead developer — created the impression that PMR would be groundbreaking and virtually unbeatable in the genre.
However, the final product does not come close to those claims. From a player’s perspective, the marketing felt full of big promises with very little substance behind them. The gap between what was said and what was delivered is so extreme that many players, myself included, perceive it as bordering on misleading.

Pricing:
Charging 60 euros or more for a product in this condition is very difficult to justify. It leaves players with the strong impression that they paid full price for something that resembles early access rather than a finished game.

PMR clearly has potential, but in its current state it is far from acceptable. I sincerely hope these issues are acknowledged and addressed, because right now the release quality and the communication leading up to it feel deeply disappointing.

Kind regards

Nach fast 1,5 Stunden Spielzeit und dem Testen mehrerer Fahrzeuge folgt hier meine Review zu Project Motor Racing.

[b]Fahrgefühl und Sound:[/b]
Das Fahrverhalten ist weit von gut entfernt. Selbst mit warmen Reifen fühlt sich alles schwammig an, als würde man über Seife rutschen. Fühlt sich weder nach Simulation, noch nach Arcade an. Dazu kommt, dass in manchen Außenansichten plötzlich der Cockpitsound abgespielt wird, was das ohnehin unausgereifte Gesamtbild noch verstärkt. Insgesamt wirkt weder das Handling noch das Sounddesign wirklich durchdacht oder fertig.

[b]Gegner:[/b]
Die KI der Gegner erinnert eher an das Niveau von 2010. Gegner fahren stur ihre Linie, reagieren kaum auf die Umgebung und weichen so gut wie nie aus. Stattdessen wird man abgedrängt oder die KI fährt einem einfach hinten drauf. Es wirkt tatsächlich so, als wäre die KI kaum getestet worden oder man hätte sie in diesem Zustand einfach akzeptiert nach dem Motto: "Wird schon passen." Tut es aber nicht.

[b]Performance:[/b]
In puncto Performance kann ich leider nicht viel Positives sagen. Selbst mit aktueller High-End-Hardware wie einem Ryzen 9 7950X3D, 96 GB RAM und einer RTX 4090 merkt man deutlich, dass das Spiel nicht rund läuft. Es kommt zu Rucklern und insgesamt wirkt alles technisch unfertig. Von Optimierung kann hier kaum die Rede sein. Für ein vollpreisiges Rennspiel mit entsprechenden Ambitionen ist das schlicht enttäuschend.

[b]Schaltung & Steuerung:[/b]
Die Automatik schafft es nicht, in den Rückwärtsgang zu schalten. Damit könnte man vielleicht leben, wenn der Rest funktionieren würde, aber selbst im normalen Fahrbetrieb werden die Gänge oft nicht sauber heruntergeschaltet. Dadurch fährt man ständig in unpassenden Gängen rum, was das ohnehin schwache Fahrgefühl noch weiter verschlechtert und viel Zeit kostet. Das Fahren per Gamepad selber ist okay, da habe ich schon schlimmeres erlebt.

[b]Grafikqualität:[/b]
Für ein Spiel, das Ende 2025 erschienen ist, wirkt die Grafik von Project Motor Racing altbacken. Vieles sieht aus wie aus einer älteren Generation (2010-2014). 
Texturen tauchen plötzlich auf, das LOD wirkt unfertig und hier und da zeigen sich Grafikfehler. Selbst auf Ultra wirken die Wolken und der Rückspiegel nicht wirklich hochwertig. Ich bin absolut kein Grafikfetischist, aber da wäre auf jeden Fall mehr möglich gewesen.
Ein weiterer nerviger Punkt: Die Maus bleibt während der Fahrt ständig im Bild. Das stört, lenkt ab und sollte in einem Rennspiel nicht passieren. Die Maus müsste beim Fahren automatisch ausgeblendet werden.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Unterm Strich wirkt Project Motor Racing wie ein Early-Access-Titel, der noch einiges an Arbeit benötigt. Das eigentliche Problem: Das Spiel ist gestern voll veröffentlicht worden und muss sich deshalb auch einer entsprechend Bewertung/Erwartungshaltung stellen. Für 30€, Early Access und ganz anderen Ambitionen wäre das alles okay gewesen, aber für 60€ nicht.

I preface this by saying I'm not adept at racing games, so I cannot give an opinion about technical aspects regarding driving mechanics or car physics. I was willing to give a sim racer a chance regardless. So, this review is more about how the game itself functions, rather than how the driving is. Other reviews can cover for that aspect.

That being said, Project Motor Racing outside of racing is quite the mess. This game launches without audio for me, which means that's a lot away immediately when I can't discern how my vehicle is doing based on hearing alone. I play with a controller, the beginner I am, so vibration would be helpful feedback as well, but there's none of that either. Thus I'm left to rely completely on the HUD and visuals.

The visuals are just alright and I get high framerates on 4070 Super, but they are not stable. Changing graphical settings causes the game to freeze, AI drivers passing me causes the game to freeze, and sometimes it just freezes because it feels like it. Oftentimes the game freezes, for what feels like a minute, and I find myself outside of the track facing the opposite direction when it resumes. The lighting is ugly, some lightsources reflecting off of wet road in massive, blurry blobs.

I can't imagine buying this for 59,99€, or 90€ with day 1 DLCS and season pass, in its current state. Incredibly, this game struggles harder than AAA UE5 titles I've reviewed. Performance is absolute bottom tier and the game has no sound for me. I would not suggest buying it right now.

1.5.0.5 Update: Straight4 are proving that they will put in the time to fix this game given the amount of the updates we have had since release. A lot of the big issues from launch are addressed, car physics generally feel a lot better.

Positives are the roster of cars is fantastic, there is a diverse range of GT race cars to choose from and a good range of tracks. Another big positive is that this game supports private peer to peer hosted lobbies letting you easily race with your mates, I know a lot of "hardcore" Sim racers think that the concept of having fun casually is a joke but not enough games support this anymore. 

Overall I hope this game succeeds in the long-run, in the short term it's not entirely there but it's on the right track.

Due to the hype, a lot was expected from this release and it is fair to say that we have been left disappointed in many areas. Perhaps the publisher wanted to differentiate themselves from the other EA SIM racing titles by releasing a full game?
A lot of these points have been made by other reviewers or influencers, but here's my take.
One of the biggest issues for me is the AI's awareness. It genuinely feels like the AI cars don't know that you're on the same track. Due to this, it's impossible to race fairly and cleanly.
This brings me on to the penalty system, which gives you time penalties when you're forced off track and damage penalties when the AI just rams into you. What happened to track limit warnings before penalties are issued?
The graphics / textures may not be cutting edge, but they do the job and the track and car models do look great. The grass looks amazing and is the best I've seen in any SIM.
I've seen many comments complaining that the FFB is dull and has no feeling. When I first played the game, I had similar thoughts. However, after watching Gamer Muscle's video on PMR Perfect FFB and playing about with the settings myself, I have to say that the FFB in this game is some of the best I've used. This just goes to show that you shouldn't jump to conclusions!
In terms of performance, again I've seen people complaining about low framerates when using high end hardware. I'm not saying that there isn't a fundamental CPU usage issue, but with a 7800X3D and a 4070 Ti Super, I'm getting 75fps on maxed out GFX settings (including 200% draw distance) without using DLSS. When I do use DLSS Quality, I get close to 100fps and when using x2 FG, I get north of 150fps.
During my 6hrs of playtime, I've only driven a handful of the cars available, but I've thoroughly enjoyed them all with their individual characteristics. I have to say that driving a GT1 Viper around Sebring was one of the most fun experiences that I've had in SIM racing. I mostly play on a 32" flat monitor and the sense of speed was amazing!
One of the biggest disappointments was the omission of VR support. AC EVO proved how much of a disaster it can be to introduce a feature that is nowhere near ready. So hopefully the PMR team are working hard to implement VR sooner rather than later.
I could go on with the positives and negatives and why you should or shouldn't buy this game. At the end of the day, no SIM racing title was ever perfect when it was first released and no SIM racing title is perfect now e.g. the completely overrated iRacing. When you buy these games, you're in it for the long haul to provide constructive feedback to the developers and shape the games future. People who just write $%"£ reviews make this niche hobby stale!

Can I recommend the the true successor to Project CARS 2? Yes, absolutely. Automobilista 2 is a very detailed, stable, and sim-serious title with a long term future and one of the most impressive vehicle and circuit rosters on the market.

This, PMR, however, is a halfway between PCARS 2... and the woeful PCARS 3. In time, once this thing is properly optimised (which it is far from right now), it will claim the crown as king of the simcades. PMR's direct competition is Forza Motorsport, Gran Turismo, and Codemasters GRID... with more car variety (not just the current GT-variant/LMDh roster), this will prove to be the better title in that market space.

Interface, stabliity. and optimisation issues aside on a first-week-of-release game that is going for an extraordinarily high price tag. (I prepurchased the Year 1 bundle from GreenManGaming for less than what the base game was marked as on the post-day-1 price hike, here on Steam).... those issues aside on what should be a crisp, not-EarlyAccess release, these are the basic red flags to be aware of for serious sim racers. I've done enough sim racing to know how to test a new racer within 30 minutes of loading.

NO ENGINE MAPPING. ABS, TC, Brake Bias, Regen.. those are bindable. No engine map changes while driving. No multi-TC or ABS system bindings either. So don't expect truely complex adjustments mid lap.
NO ENGINE START bindings. Not that I personally care for this one, but the omission speaks volumes that this is not a serious sim. You  clearly don't need to start/restart your engine because there will never be a risk of stalling.
HUD = Basic. Very simcade in options. You may be able to adjust the layout like AMS2, but the info on hand feels very streamlined in a way that is disappointing for serious sim racers, but plenty fine for a simcade experience.
IMPACT SOUND FX = Seriously, this triggered my rage. Like the weird "BADOING" that PCARS 3 had... any and every impact has a generic "KAPAP" sound that made me think I was button mashing Punch buttons on Street Fighter 2 Turbo as a kid in the 90's on an ole arcade machine.
NO HELMET VIEW. Just your basic cockpit view among the basic singular Bumper / Hood / Cockpit / Roof / 3rd Person selections. Not as restrictive as PCARS 3, but definitely not AMS2 or even PCARS 2 in terms of choice. Move your seating position too far back and you will start seeing your avatar's body/helmet clipping into camera view.
VISUALS = Are nice enough, but not competitive by 2025 standards, and still chugs due to to poor Day 1 optimisation. Details are lacking though. Try racing in the heaivest of rain, your mirror view will have ZERO spray back and the track surface is dry, which is unsettling. Visibility is also very accessible, like Forza Motorsport 8, and not the suicidal death fest of "Thunderstorm" in the more serious sim racers like AMS2, or even AC-Competizione.

First load on my ultrawide screen setup had the game locked into a 16:9 Borderless Fullscreen mode with the Settings button (on the menu) right at the bottom right and completely inaccesssible because the Windows Taskbar was blocking access to anyhing that appears at the bottom... and things like RACE or APPROVE or whatever are situated at the bottom. I had to button mash my way into an active race weekend to finally find access to the Settings from a menu option rather than an icon hidden behind the Task Bar. Changing resolution required a full restart of the game client.. Multiple Red Flags here.

Everything with my Simucube 2 Pro DDU, Cube Controls F-Pro wheel and Heusinkveld pedals bound perfectly fine. My cheap Chinee H-shifter and hand brakes also recognised and bound fine. A proper FFB profile will take some dialing in. It won't be the unique pain that PCARS/AMS2 was/is to setup... but on my brutally overpowered, wrist breaking RaceRoom profile... it is clear that there is a lot less nuanced telemtry being communicated to the wheel. Made me think of the workarounds Simucube owners have to make to get Forza Horizon games to work, and what that feels like.

My F-Pro wheel... genuinely makes me feel sad, because it is wasted on this game. Over half of the buttons and dials on my wheel have absolutely no purpose because this game does not provide me with enough "things" to need to bind.

I have no regrets about owning this, though it definitely has proven to be yet another irresponsible and wasteful "Preorder" not worthy of day 1 pricing. But in the war of sim racing... Assetto Corsa EVO has already won, in every aspect from car roster to physics to visual immersion... to value for money and confidence that it has a long term future of support.

I say the following as one of the many original backers and Alpha-onwards-testers of PCARS 1.... Wait until this thing gets SteamDeck approval as your proof that the game has been optimised enough, is worthy of either a gamepad or entry level (plastic Thrustmaster/Logitech) wheels... and is on special down the line. Unless there are rumours of a sequel. If there is a hint that this thing ever receives a sequel, then accept that this is a pump and dump IP.

If you have spent stupid money on a hardcore rig like I have... move along, nothing to see here.

To start, I refunded because I wanted to get the full bundle however the way steam has it bundled will not allow you to complete the purchase since the Group 5 car pack is included in the season 1 expansion and individually. I ultimately purchased it through the Microsoft store because their bundling worked, but I felt like I needed to leave a review for it. 

I wouldn't read too much into all the negativity. Everyone is quick to jump on the bash wagon. I understand that when a game is released it should be in a good position already, and overall I think this one is and there is no reason to believe the devs won't release patches to make it even better. 

The sound of this game is top notch. You actually feel like you are in the car and on the track. The head movement while driving add to the immersion and realism. The graphics are good but a bit underwhelming honestly. Especially in menus when selecting cars, something is just off about it.

This game seems to be the most realistic with it tire model and the necessity of getting both brakes and tires up to their temp window before going to a push lap, if not, you will be the car through the lap. In addition, when following too close to cars ahead you will get in their dirty air and you will feel that through the turns making the car a bit more unpredictable through them, but this is also the only game I have ever played that seems to get that extremely well. You can feel the front end get light and lose causing understeer and its just great. 

That being said, yes, there definitely needs to be some work on the AI models, primarily those surrounding spacial awareness and the seemingly bump in speed they have compared you. 

I have yet to play anything in the rain (can't actually find that right now), and the menu UI seems a bit bland compared to the Project CARS series that this hails from. 

It's a bit weird that some of the real tracks use the real names and others do not. Likely because of licensing, or lack thereof? 

One note is I did need to tweak the FFB settings since out of the box it was way too low. It was odd that the stock settings was 100 for FFB and I needed to crank up to 200 for it to feel good. I am using a Fanatec Podium DD1 Base for anyone curious.

Whether you get it now or wait, hang in there as I am certain this game will get better with upcoming patches and content releases.

I’m gonna say it… I actually don’t mind this game — I kinda like it. Yeah, the price is ridiculous for something that still feels unfinished, and launching with DLC right out of the gate is wild. But putting that aside, the game itself feels solid. I’ve mostly been sticking to the GTO and GT1 classes, and once you get the hang of them, they’re genuinely fun to drive.

Honestly, I think the hype train did more harm than good. Expectations were so sky-high that no game was ever going to hit them. I still remember LMU at launch — it was a straight-up mess, but look at it now: easily one of the best sims out there. PMR has that same kind of potential, especially with mod support. There are some insanely talented modders in this community, and that alone could elevate the game into real contender territory.

So here’s my take: if you can grab it on sale like I did, it’s worth giving a shot. Performance isn’t amazing, but at least the AI has improved a lot with the latest update.

So a rouuuuuught start, as i think one or two reviewers might have mentioned.

It's way off yet but if you're willing to be patient, I do think it'll get there, and i believe S4S are going to stick at it, because i've seen nothing to suggest they won't. I'm not interested in boarding the IB hate train, and i'll be honest, in interviews i quite like him. Don't mistake launch bugs for a lack of passion or care, this stuff is insanely complicated, and if people want to be in denial about that over $35 (easily found right now and almost EA pricing) it's up to them but it doesn't change that fact. It genuinely does quite a lot right, driving can feel really quite fun/exhilarating and the cockpits are cool with a sense of depth not often seen. Really enjoying the sound design too. The AI is.....aggressive in its approach right now.

The graphics are bit at odds at times; it's capable of looking really quite good but then you see things like the clouds during rain at sunset and man, i'm not sure what's going on with that, it would be better to have none as they're so blurry in constrast with the sharpness of the ground that it's actually visually distracting. It doesn't seem possible to recreate some of the atmospheric conditions seen in the promo videos, at least not with the same  fidelity (eg nurburgring wet at night). Rain through the sunvisor isn't a showstopper, but it's hard to overlook. Sebring etc look really quite cool and alive, and the track rubber, birds etc all give it a sense of being a living track. One thing i will say is i don't think i've played anything on PC that's felt so much like it has a bit of Gran Turismo to it when in the slower cars, and i mean that as a compliment ironically to the standards GT goes for. The MX5 on lime rock absolutely gave me those vibes in the best possible way and it's moments like that you realise they are indeed on to something here.

It's best to consider it a hotlapper right now whilst they iron out AI, optimisation etc so to say it's unplayable would be overstating a bit. There's lots of polish and fix, but the patches are already goling head on at things.

People rightly have complaints, but it's not a write off by a long shot, even if people have some weird desire to actually see it be. I'm not sure where that would leave us with new Sims going forward if the attitude is anything less than perfect (and this is much less right now) is a crime. Games rarely launch finished anymore. You don't get many Arc Raiders/Finals. It sucks, but it's across the board.

My rating is a neutral as it's based on what you're willing to buy into, but i have to pick yes or no i'll pick yes, honestly. If you know you're willing to be patient jump in and enjoy what's there with a view of where it'll go, if not (and that's fine, but it's public knowledge what you're in for at this point) probably better to give it 12 months and save yourself the headache.

Ich fahre seit Jahren Sim Racing. Meine Lieblingssims sind rF2 und Raceroom. Auch iRacing kann ich was abgewinnen. Nur um das Ganze ein bisschen einzuordnen. Project Cars 1 und 2 fand ich richtig, richtig schlecht. Die SME hat sogar in AMS2 ganz lange nicht funktioniert. Alles hat sich wie auf Schienen angefühlt. Auch anfangs in AMS2. Reiza hat Jahre gebraucht, um die Sim ansatzweise ans Laufen zu bringen. Und dann kommt PMR. 

[b]Was habe ich ganz zu Anfang gehofft? [/b]
- Eine Sim wir GTR2 zu bekommen. Doch als dann klar wurde, dass das Ding Crossplay haben soll, war eigentlich schon klar, dass hier doch wieder was in Richtung PC1 und 2 kommen wird. 

[b]Was haben wir bekommen?[/b] 
- Eine Simulation, die keine Hardcore Simulation ist. Aber trotzdem: PMR fühlt sich jetzt schon weitaus nachvollziehbarer an, als PC es jemals war. 

[b]Was mich stört:[/b]
 - Mein Shifter wird erkannt, ich kann ihn aber nicht mappen. Mal sehen, ob da noch ein Update kommt. 
- Zudem habe ich einen seltsamen Bug: Ich muss in jedem Menu-Schritt einmal auf die Tastatur drücken, weil ich sonst im Menu sich immer alles so verhält, als würde ich die Taste "Nach unten" gedrückt halten. 
- Noch kein Triple-Screen-Support. Die Auflösung wird unterstützt. Mehr aber leider nicht. 

Ich versuche den Hate mal ein bisschen einzuordnen: 
[b]"Die Spiegel sehen bescheiden aus."[/b] - Tun sie. Zumindest der virtuelle Spiegel. Er sieht halt so aus, wie er in ACC immer ausgesehen hat. Da hat niemand gemeckert. 

[b]"Das ist eine Early Access. Keine Vollversion!" [/b]- Ja. Es ist noch nicht fertig. Hätten sie es als EA herausgebracht, wäre das Geschrei auch wieder groß gewesen. Riesengroß sogar. Hier hätte man durchaus das Label "EA" draufpacken sollen. Ich denke, dass hätte PMR weitaus besser getan.

[b]"Die Physik ist bescheiden!" [/b]- Ist sie nicht. Zumindest weitaus intuitiver und besser umgesetzt als in  PC. Man merkt, was die Autos machen. Auf den Kerbs fühlt es sich genial an. Kommt man auf die Wiese, muss man ackern. Kommt man ins Kies, wird man hart abgebremst. Verliert man das Heck, kann man es einfangen, wenn man es nicht übertreibt.

[b]"Die Performance ist unter aller Sau!"[/b] - Sie ist nicht gut. Aber unter aller Sau ist sie auch nicht. Hier wird hoffentlich noch gepatcht. Aber es ist durchaus Spielbar. Ich hatte keine Frame-Einbrüche und nichts. 

[b]"Das FFB ist bescheiden!"[/b] - Es ist nicht. Das FFB ist gut. Wheelbases brauchen Updates. Wahrscheinlich liegt es an den Settings. ALLES ist nachvollziehbar. Bei meiner Simagic Base out of the box. 

[b]"Die Grafik sieht aus, wie auf der PS2!" [/b]- Nein. Tut sie nicht. Konsoleros werden hier wahrscheinlich GT7 als Vergleich nehmen. GT7 ist meiner Meinung nach das grafisch beste Rennspiel auf dem Markt. Da haben wahrscheinlich tausende Leute dran gearbeitet. Und es musste nur für eine Konsole optimiert werden. Der Vergleich ist also Unsinn. PMR sieht auch nicht so gut aus, wie AMS2. Aber mit LMU kann es durchaus mithalten. Da meckert seltsamerweise auch wieder keiner. 

[b]"Die KI ist bescheiden!" [/b]- Ja. Volltreffer. Ist sie. Hier müssen noch viele Updates folgen. Aber: In PC2 hat die KI es zu Release teilweise nicht über die Startlinie geschafft. Da wurde es aber nicht halb so heftig kritisiert wie hier.  

[b]"Beim Bremsen kommt das Heck!"[/b] - Ja. Tut es. Zwischengas automatisch einstellen und auf ein Update warten. Es fährt sich mit automatischem Zwischengas aber gut. 

[b]Was bleibt?[/b] 
- Eine Simulation mit sehr viel Potential. Leider wird sie komplett madig geredet - was sie meiner Meinung nach aber nicht verdient hat. Zumindest nicht, wenn man den Kern der Sim betrachtet: Eine Sim, die immer nachvollziehbar ist und sich jetzt schon weitaus griffiger und dynamischer anfühlt, als es PC jemals getan hat. 

Nachts ist die Beleuchtung noch ein bisschen unstimmig. Aber: Die Scheinwerfer der anderen Autos scheinen richtig in den Wald hinein. Das hat ACC nie gehabt. Dort wurde nur der eigene Scheinwerfer korrekt simuliert. Was ich immer sehr störend und als wenig immersiv empfunden habe. Das ist hier schon weitaus besser. 

[b]Was mir noch gut gefällt: [/b]
- Die Idee, einen Online-Führerschein zu machen. Da werde ich noch mit experimentieren - falls man Leute zum online fahren findet. 
- Die Sounds der Autos sind absolut super. 

[b]Was ich absolut seltsam finde:[/b] 
- AUF EINMAL, redet es jeder Youtuber schlecht. Es ist nicht mehr und nicht weniger als ein Hype, auf den aufgesprungen wird, im Klicks zu generieren. PMR kann man jetzt schon einiges abgewinnen. Mal sehen, was die kommenden Updates so bringen. 

Ich freu mich jetzt schon drauf.

[b]Update #1: [/b]
Der Grund, warum der Spiegel so bescheiden aussieht nennt sich DLSS. Schaltet man DLSS aus, sieht der Spiegel sofort um einiges besser aus. Auch als beispielsweise in ACC.
DLSS ist einfach immer ein Kompromiss. Es soll alte Hardware dazu bringen, neue Spiele oder Grafikmonster (z.B.: Cyperpunk mit RT) überhaupt spielbar zu machen. DLSS sieht in fast jedem Spiel bescheiden aus. So auch hier. Man hat also einen Kompromiss (DLSS) dafür verantwortlich gemacht, die Spiegel schlecht zu machen. Auch interessant, dass man bemerkt, dass sich Rezensenten gar nicht erst mit dem Spiel auseinandersetzen, sondern direkt den Daumen nach unten geben...
